records.title: infinite
records.note:
What if you could meet your past or future self across space and time. What might you advise, observe, affirm, or say to yourself ?

One truth I would reveal to my past self is: 
you will use your voice and your journal entries will become poems, stories will become speeches, and songs will spring forth into the world to become your legacy. 

“Infinite” is a dance between my past, present, and future self. If we see more limitlessly we find that time is in fact not short, time is abundant as well, life is the longest dance we will ever know.   

The world is what it is, for better or worse because people shaped it so, that being said, I believe we are in an everlasting cycle of co-creation with the universe. “Infinite” asks us to get on the dancefloor ( a metaphor for life) and tap in with self and one another to create the world we want to live in and leave behind for future  generations. 

Art imitates life and life imitates art. Dreams are sacred and I believe we don’t quit until we’ve lived each one. 

Produced by New Orleans royalty, Ciara Porter( granddaughter of George Porter Jr. , The Meters) , recorded at House of Corperning with her partner, Charles aka Winowilly ( from Philly) and mixed & mastered by Future Surf  Labs founder Cam Murdoch, the song is made up of bars, bounce, melodic house poly-rhythms, and soulful dance breaks. 

Everyday I reaffirm to present self that I am surrounded by supportive community, I can step out of my way and let the blessings flow into my life. 
Breathe now look up, look within, and look how far we’ve come. 

If I met my future self, I would encourage her to  continue to enjoy the fruits of her labor and to keep finding ways to honor all the people she has encountered along the way, they have  all mattered.

I am inspired daily and have so much love for so many of you in ways that don’t even belong to me🙏🏾

Infinite gratitude,

✨Charm

records.title: Be Here Long
records.note:
This record is dedicated to my brother.
River Naim Harris
#FreeRio

We all process our trauma differently, and the past few years of my life have been quite traumatic. On one hand I understand that I am not defined by these traumas. They are a part of my journey but they do not make me who I am. Yet, on the other hand I understand that in order for me to heal I need to address them. To process them. To find acceptance. To find forgiveness. To find peace.

The fact that songwriting is a gift is not something that’s lost on me. I am grateful every day to be able to express myself through music in a way that helps me heal. I don’t know a better way to communicate. I don’t know a better form of therapy than being completely vulnerable: on record. 

I wrote “Be Here Long” at one of the lowest points in my life. At the time I didn’t realize how many emotions I was suppressing and how much of an impact it was having on me. It’s funny how art reflects life because I feel like I was in autopilot both mentally and musically. I didn’t need to force this record and truthfully, I don’t feel like [I] wrote it; it wrote itself. I just remember pacing around my apartment in tears and finally looking down at a finished song.

One section in particular resonated with me at a core level:

“You halfway through a sentence, and it’s harder to keep dreaming.
I’m halfway through a sentence, and it’s harder to keep reading.
Letters feel like packages whenever I’m receiving… heavy.

I feel the distance, the dissonance
The disconnect from your innocence
The tears, rain…
The pain in your eyes, the resemblance
Liquor in my cup, a deliverance
And liquor on the ground in remembrance”

It reminded me that we’re all fighting our individual battles. Together. We are all fighting to maintain our light. To keep going on days where it may seem hopeless. To find love in all that we do. I am not physically with my brother but his battle is my battle. His light is my light. His peace is my peace. And we will find it together.

I thought a lot about what I wanted my initial offering for this platform to be. Full transparency, it gave me a lot of anxiety trying to pick the “perfect” song. I never set out to make any type of record. I just create what I feel called to create. But I found hope in this record. And that’s something I’d love to contribute to my people in any way possible.

I love you guys. Thank you for changing my life. Thank you for reminding me of my worth when I forget. Thank you f

records.title: Synchronize (RAC Mix)
records.note:
It’s crazy how time flies. It feels like yesterday that we started writing songs together in high school, recording our songs at Clemens’ house and just uploading it for the world to hear. But already almost ten years have passed since we released our first album and we are grateful for every single step in our journey till today, honored that we are still here and able to do what we love.

And we’re hoping that we can do this for much longer, but while writing ‘Synchronize’ we did have some apocalyptic images in our heads. We liked the idea of coming from the „smoke in the sky“  image - that was there first - and to pair that with the comfort of being totally in love/synchronization and the absurdity it creates. Even though this world seems to be going down slowly, if you find yourself in sync with a person you love or in sync with the world around you, it resembles the blind feeling of love and how that can make you „blind“ for other real happenings. Like seeing everything through rose-colored glasses. Making you feel good endlessly.

We are so delighted that RAC, an artist we always admired for his unique sound and creativity, took our song and made his own version of it. RAC really did a beautiful job on reinterpreting our song. The Song structure itself didn‘t change but the world he built around it, so it feels more like a remake than a remix. His guitar playing and new harmonies take the song to another level in a more dark and melancholic way and we really love how it turned out. From bottom to top a little masterpiece.

records.title: Affirmations
records.note:
“If you were given the ear of every living being on this earth for 5 minutes, what would you say?” 
This is a question that (whether consciously or unconsciously) lingers at the back of my mind every time  I create any art. I operate in a space of gratitude and abundance, thankful for the gifts I’ve been given from the source. Thankful for my journey, my story and for the ancestors that came before me. I’m nothing without my community. I’ve learned that true growth doesn’t occur in a vacuum and I know that I’m constantly being poured into because I pour into others. It’s a cycle of love. I know all too well the importance of my purpose (while here in the physical) and the exact responsibility I have to live in that purpose. I’m a builder, simple as that. It's that ideology that's driven me since I was a kid and the ethos that acts as the fuel to my fire as a Cameroonian-American, multi-disciplined creative, an advocate for my community and a bridge between the diaspora and the motherland.

“Affirmations” is self love personified and a real time case study for the power of community. This happens to be the first song of five that I recorded during a live stream with the incredibly talented June Jissle and two of his frequent collaborators, Big Racco & Tito G. I had the pleasure of meeting June (via my good brother, Cam Murdoch) back in March at the start of what we now call Future Surf Radio and I instantly became a fan. Fast forward 6 months later I know have the pleasure of calling him my brother. June called me with an idea one night that I was immediately down for. He wanted to do a challenge where he would have 15 minutes to star production and pass it along to the next person who then had 15 minutes to contribute and then finally I would have 20 mins to load the production and create a song. We did this process live and in a little under 3 hours we ended up creating an EP full of self-love, confidence, culture and vision.

I’ve been in a state of flow and this process documented that stream of consciousness. June is nothing short of a genius and this record would have never happened with out him. I’m grateful to be able to use this song as an opportunity to bring not only, Tito & Racco into the world of Web 3 but my brother, Ashton Woods, who mixed and mastered the record. This song reminds you that no dream is too big and you deserve to have good things. Please set the tone for growth and success in your life by calling to it.

I hope you enjoy.

Wit

Hiii, we are KarmaVioletta! We're a traveling music duo couple, involved in the Web3, creator & wellness spaces. We believe in a world where a kid can tell their parents, "I want to be a musician, artist or creator," & there's a viable path to that. We were formed in 2019 in Miami, after we fell in love and started creating in our home studio. We feel that we are all in this human experience together, so let's dance :)

Karma, born in Vancouver, raised in Hawaii & Miami, comes from a musical family, having learned to play the drums at age 3, followed by guitar, singing & piano. In 2012, he first discovered Ableton and that took him down the rabbit hole, which he re-surfaced from as a producer, singer/ songwriter, sound engineer & DJ.      Violetta (Vee-oh-letta), born in Germany, raised in Russia & America, learned to play the piano & guitar at a young age. She’s been singing her whole life & started songwriting in 2017, which also led her into co-producing & DJing.

This is our very first drop on Sound.xyz from our duo project. We got into Web3 via Karma.wav red-pilling Violetta at NFT NYC last year, Nov 2021. During that trip, we met up with the Songcamp fam IRL & had our first studio session together. We are now both a part of their most recent camp of 77 members, Camp Chaos, the headless band. Right around that same time we started wavWRLD, through which we are building infrastructure to enable unique musical experiences that connect artists with their true fans.

We wrote this song in the beginning of our relationship, about 3 years ago. It encompasses those moments of butterflies & excitement, but slight fear at the same time, when you realize that you’ve already fallen so deeply for this person, your person. “So Deep” also represents gratitude for all that has come beforehand, including past relationships, as they were filled with hard lessons that prepared you & got you to where you are now, with who you are now. They got you to a much better place. Only you know what’s best for you, so trust yourself & remember to do you & love YOU first, then everything else will fall into place.

Thank you so much for listening, being a part of our journey & collecting.

records.title: Back on the Fence (Original Demo)
records.note:
My relationship with music is always changing. I picked up the guitar 10 years ago out of necessity; life was beginning to flood with new emotions and experiences, and I desperately needed an outflow. With time, songs eventually became a second language, lending me the keys to new friendships and identity within self expression. In 2018, I had all but sold my soul to the medical field for a doctorate in physical therapy when music exerted it’s force on me again, this time pulling me away from medicine and into the thicket of my creative journey. Nowadays music is my religion, and songwriting feels a lot like meditation. The creative process is both merciless and vigilant—it casts it’s light into my darkest corners. What started as an outlet has become the setting for confronting the parts of myself I fear the most.

This demo of ‘Back on the Fence’ is a testament to the power of songwriting as a spiritual guide. I have trouble following through on positive change, and I think writing this song helped me gain a sense for when I start to regress into old thought patterns and behaviors—things like self-isolation, splitting hairs over the smallest stuff, or ironically losing weeks of life at a time to the thought of eventually dying. I’m really so thankful for the opportunity to rediscover this demo and share it. Letting go of it has allowed me to honor and appreciate every step in my creative process.

records.title: Personally
records.note:
Emily Lazar is a multi-disciplinary artist fronting the rock/metal transmedia project, September Mourning. She made history as the first female metal/ hard rock musician to mint and sell an NFT on the blockchain. She has spoken about her accomplishments in Web 3/ NFT's at Harvard (2x), NFT.NYC and ETH Denver Conferences.

September Mourning is a transmedia project based on a comic book series she wrote and published through Image/Top Cow Comics with her business partner Marc Silvestri (Batman/Witchblade/Darkness). September Mourning is the title character. As a human reaper hybrid, she  gives expired souls a second chance at life in another body. In doing so, she messes with  the plans of the antagonist, Fate, who is trying to rid  earth of all the good souls and leave the bad so the world will self-destruct and It can start anew. An epic war between the living and the dead ensues. Emily plays the title character on stage.

Emily designed the world she and her band (Rich Juzwick, Kyle Mayer and Aaron Hoover) bring to life on stage, including costumes, choreography, sets, etc. The band has toured with & opened festivals for Rob Zombie, Marilyn Manson, Slipknot, Mudvayne and others across Europe and the United States.

The high energy hard rock anthem, “Personally” slaps you in the face with driving guitars, percussion and vocals fueled by rage. The lyrics mimic the anger September feels towards Fate in the story  but can very easily be relatable to any listener’s real life frustrations as well. 

Wes Henry brilliantly captures the energy and emotion of the song in his album artwork.

Album Art: Wes Henry
Song Credits: September Mourning Collective

records.title: Submersion
records.note:
Hi! My name is Brij, I’m a producer, DJ and music teacher from Mumbai and I’ve been making tunes across genres for close to 7 years, mainly under the name Three Oscillators. I’ve been influenced by science fiction, dystopia and electronic music ever since I was a kid, and I bring out these influences in the music I make.

While being a producer, I also DJ under the same name and have played some of the wildest gigs in my home country of India, a place with a small, niche audience that absorbs everything from techno, drum n’ bass and RnB to even more experimental genres.

Dreamy, introspective and emotional are some words I’d describe most of my music with, and I see every tune of mine as an inward journey into your consciousness. Submersion is my first tune on Sound and marks almost a year of being into web3 and music NFTs, something that has changed my life and I’m truly grateful for. This journey has had its ups and downs but that’s a story for another day.

Submersion is about immersing yourself in your thoughts and letting them consume you completely. I went on a trip to Goa last year and experienced bioluminescence for the first time in my entire life; watching the ocean glow while you swim in it is an unparalleled experience. A few tunes I’ve made after that trip attempt to encapsulate that feeling, and Submersion is one of them. I haven’t decided on what to do with these tunes yet - it might be a single or end up becoming an EP. As a collector, you’ll be the first to know what I do with them!

I hope you enjoy the music and I hope it makes you feel something. Now close your eyes…

Until next time <3

records.title: How To Be Us
records.note:
How To Be Us was Written, Produced and Arranged by Saint Rien.

About me? Man, I just fucking love creating and consuming art. I'm unhealthily obsessed.

I am a 5th generation performer and have jumped into all the creative endeavors that have presented themselves to me. I grew up acting, joined a band when I was 16 and at the same time I was modeling commercial, runway and editorial. I then switched to creative directing and styling in fashion too. 

After the band split up I slept on couch pillows for six months in my friend's studio and learned how to produce before spending every cent I had on a visa to move to America. Two weeks before my flight, I met her…

She was and will always be the most beautiful person I’ve ever seen, Stephanie… Even a french name! From the day we first met, we didn’t leave each other's side for over a week. It felt impossible to imagine not being together, I had real thoughts of struggling to remember life without her even though that reality was merely days prior.

How To Be Us is a retrospective song looking back at every moment of those first months together. Falling for her, feeling like we wouldn't be able to be together, moving across the world and finally proposing to her after six months… I wanted to capture the duality of how it felt to meet the love of your life as you were planning to leave and never come back. I hope you enjoy. 🥀

records.title: CRYSTAL CAVERNS
records.note:
Hi I'm Luca. I used to say I was just a producer, then just a DJ, but only now do I feel like I fully encompass the role of an artist. I've spent the last 10 years navigating the electronic music space to varying degrees of success while using SoundCloud and digital distribution platforms as a digital diary to share my eclectic productions with the world. Through a series of fortuitous events, persistence and a dedication to the craft I found myself touring the globe over selling out hard ticket shows a world away from my tiny apartment in Brooklyn where it all started. 

That all came to a screeching halt with  the pandemic, although covid gave me a much needed reprieve from touring nonstop and allowed me to re-evaluate what it was that I wanted to do with music. I briefly pivoted into more rave centric music with a project centered entirely around speedhouse music but, without any raves to play the tour we had scheduled around the material was postponed until outright cancelled. 

During this period of particular financial uncertainty I was introduced to the NFT space through my friends cooper and Kris (wuki). I became heavily involved in several project, teaching myself JavaScript and python in order to fully dive into generative art and music creation. At some point I realized that despite my enthusiasm for learning a diverse new skill set I was drifting farther away from the thing that gave me true purpose in life - that of creating and sharing music.
 
It was during this time I penned Crystal Caverns. I hadn't touched upon the style that had so fortuitously brought me to this point in some time - after years of production experience I was coming back with both a fresh ears and a fresh heart to fully embrace the sound. Although I have since pivoted out into more mature techno leanings I felt like a more melodic superfluous future bass romper was the perfect fit for a sound.xyz drop.

records.title: Versions of Me
records.note:
Versions of me is the realization of it all.

So much of my life, I’ve dedicated everything I’ve had to others. Which isn’t always a bad thing…unless you never refill your own cup.

This song acknowledges out loud that all of the good coming my way, from years of hard work and pouring my heart and soul into making sure people are taken care of, is well deserved.

I acknowledge where I fell short countless times trying to be perfect and look forward to a bright future that will give me everything I need and desire because of the love I have sown. I no longer desire to be anything but the imperfect masterpiece I have been designed to be.

Written and vocally produced by Jazzi Richardson
Produced by Joshua “Tipz” Richardson
Mixed and Mastered by Joshua “Tipz” Richardson

records.title: Count
records.note:
My name is Pat Dimitri. I’ve been a professional touring guitar player, composer, and producer for 10 years. I’ve played for numerous artists, some you know, many you don’t - this career has taken me all over the world as a performer, and more importantly made me into the musician that I am. Despite having played in front of millions of people, 10 years in and I still found myself struggling for financial and creative freedom - Web3 provided a solution to this problem I have been trying to solve since before I knew blockchain existed, and that's why I've been all in on it for the past 18 months.

This record was written in 2020 where my personal frustration with misinformation was at an all time high. I felt like I needed to explore the idea of seeing things so clearly while others had obvious revelations obscured. In short, the past 5-6 years was a mind bogglingly thorough example of Dunning-Krueger, and this song proved to be an outlet for that anger - and an outlet for the legend Kwudi to drop a flawless verse.

For those that are unaware, Kwudi is one of my closest friends and has a list of accolades that would take up the entire page - most notably being an amazing solo artist and a producer for Childish Gambino. He recently found himself in a serious motorcycle accident - part of the ethos of this song is making sure that him and his family get all the help they need. Half of primary sales are going to his gofundme.

The more we know the more we know we don’t know.. but what we do know has to count for something, right?

records.title: BOOK
records.note:
Have you ever watched a movie where the masterful swordsman was simply nowhere to be found? He was perhaps tending to his garden, or building a cabin, until the people in need of rescue finally contacted him to pick his sword back up? this song is that return exactly. 

Until now, Seattle rapper, producer, cartoonist, etc. J’von had quietly stepped away from releasing music, though still recording & practicing everyday. With the successful release of Loser Club, an NFT art project designed by the man himself, he has found himself drawing more, whilst obtaining more resources than ever to really push his creative mind further. But what does he have to say? Exactly how much of himself does he have available to give now?

“BOOK” is a rap song, where j’von discusses the past, the present, and the future of who he is & is destined to be. Esotericism ensued, where only a select few will be able to resonate with his messages. j’von speaks of his bouts with depression, identity, relevance, and sabotage, but with such a slyness, who would really know?

j’von is currently recording his next album. if “BOOK” is to be any signaling of where the man is headed, then brace yourselves. It's going to be a long adventure.

records.title: best or worst?
records.note:
Hello hello, I’m Kathleen! 

I’m a Boston born independent singer/songwriter (go pats), currently residing in Nashville, TN (yeehaw?) I’ve been actively releasing music for about 10 years, but really just got into my own groove over the past few. Growing up in Massachusetts, I was deeply inspired by Irish and folk music. My dad introduced me to Alison Krauss and I’ve been writing sad shit ever since. 

This is my very first drop with Sound.xyz but my introduction to web3 came a little over a year ago. During the pandemic, I had a few sessions via zoom with my friend Matthew Chaim. At that point, his idea for Songcamp was really brewing and I could tell how excited he was for what web3 could become for independent artists. I didn’t want to miss out. I was then a part of Camp Elektra as well as the most recent camp, Camp Chaos. Songcamp became the ideal playground for me to learn & experiment in this space alongside this group of people, whom are now my family. 

I wrote this song a few months back while on tour in The Netherlands. I was experiencing, for the first time, being away from a partner and having it feel really healthy. Before this, I wasn’t used to the idea of someone fully supporting my wandering spirit or the fact that my career can take me elsewhere for weeks at a time. I also hadn't found this time away in the past to be very successful.. had been cheated on multiple times by the first guy I ever fell for, blah blah good timesssss my dudesss

“best or worst?” is my talking through that pessimistic side of me.. when I don’t mean to self sabotage, or talk myself out of enjoying the present moment.. but I do! At times when my life is going really well, I find myself being scared to get tooooo happy. It’s like my “what’s the catch?” mentality creeps (hey, therapy!!). Anyway, life is full of the push & pull of inner thoughts and I wanted to be honest about that. 


Thank you so much for being here,
and thank you Sound.xyz team for the platform x
KR

records.title: I'm With The DJ
records.note:
So I’m a DJ.

My job is to make sure you're having a good time. I select different sounds and mash them up and people actually pay me stupid money to do it.

I live for sampling. Everything is a remix.

The first time I heard “D.J. Girl” by Katalina was at a rave. For the next 10 years, I whole-heartedly believed that was the original song. (DJ Caffeine)

It wasn’t until this year that I discovered the original and as a house-head you can imagine my excitement!

I immediately started playing it in all of my sets. I found the acapella and made an edit that felt more aligned with what I play today.

I played it out and people really liked it.

I made a TikTok and it went moderately viral (for me)

Me to record labels: Hey guys do you like this song?

So I made another TikTok with an updated version. And it happened again.

Cool cool cool, so I guess I’m doing it on my own.

This is my version of I’m With the DJ.

records.title: Wa Nibi (Come Here)
records.note:
As a kid growing up in South Jersey my main music of choice was trap and club music, but as I developed as a musician and started to study other genres of music I learned to appreciate all different styles. Being a Nigerian man growing up in America, sometimes I felt like my house was Lagos Nigeria and as soon as I stepped out those doors I entered back into America and that's because of the music and culture my father gave me as a kid which helped me be the producer, dj, songwriter, and artist I am today pulling from all styles of music.

I started making music when I was 13 years old and played in different bands throughout high school with my best friends. I grew up loving punk and alt-rock music which inspired me to learn how to play the guitar. I started producing electronic music and making remixes of songs like Dr. Dre’s “The Next Episode” which exploded on Soundcloud and YouTube. I released one of my first original San Holo tracks “We Rise” in 2015 and “Light” in 2017 along with many other songs that I still play in my shows to this day. I’ve had the opportunity to tour around the world and perform at incredible venues and festivals since then. In 2018, I released my debut album titled album1 on my record label, bitbird. I found myself back in the same part of town (Echo Park) years later while I was recording my second album, bb u ok?.

One day when I got back home after a long tour, I felt inspired and I spontaneously made a little beat on my phone while laying in bed. I found this phone beat on my computer recently, I almost forgot that I made it! I really like the raw nature of this beat, it’s very unpolished and definitely not perfect... But somehow a very strong emotion shines through all the imperfections. About 95% of what you hear on this track was recorded and produced on my iPhone, including the vocals! Every person you pass by in life has their own story, in a way you might think this separates us… but actually, the opposite is true: It connects us. 

I wanted to write a song about sonder and remind myself to embrace everything that life throws my way, whether I might think it’s good or bad. Sometimes the lows in life end up being an incredible lesson that actually turns out to be a high after all. Which brings the question: What if the lows aren’t actually that bad, if you learn to accept what is. Everything you go through in life shapes you as a person. In a way you can say your memories are always a part of you… Our memories on rewind… All The Lows, All The Highs. - San Holo ↑%

records.title: JOKE
records.note:
“Joke” came to me after an unwanted encounter I recently had with my old Honor’s Chemistry teacher from high school (who I NEVER got along with). He often made passive aggressive and patronizing remarks about my passions because they were different from his. While working an odd job in May, I bumped into him, and thus came the passive aggressive remarks that he would so often make 10 years prior. He continued to insinuate that my career, work ethic, and overall presence was laughable. I played the bigger man in person, killing him with kindness, and when I got home I spazzed. But “Joke” became more than your corny “diss track to the teacher who never believed in me” type song. It became a work of art that encompassed an everlasting theme in my life. Being Yourself, and being proud of who you are. 

I realized that I have spent so much of my life here on earth wearing masks, trying to fulfill other people’s perceptions of me, only to burn out some days wondering why I’m this way… wondering who I am in general. Subconsciously, I have surrounded myself with so many people that are unapologetically themselves no matter the situation, and I’ve always admired that skill. A lot of those people have said that I exhibit that trait as well, but I’ve never felt that way about myself. Maybe I am mirroring their energy and I feel comfortable enough to shine in front of them because they showed me the way. This year, I started really listening to what THOSE people have said about me… really taking in why I am loved by my friends and why I am unique as a person. 

With “Joke” I wanted every aspect of myself to shine through the song’s production. I performed a sketch with funny voices during the intro of the track, I produced an 8-bit video game styled instrumental, I sampled my grandmother and mother, and I added an instrumental and tonal shift midway through the track. That being said, I love doing funny voices, I love video games, I love my family, and I love beat switches and moody contrast. So why not put all of those things in a song, regardless of what other people think? These are just some of the things in a long list of interests that make me: ME! And I plan on showing the rest of those special attributes throughout the rest of my career.

records.title: Higher
records.note:
‘Higher’ started in a very unusual way for me. A very, very, unusual way. My friend Salvador Breed sent me a video of a parrot vocalising / imitating a percussive rhythm. It sounded like the parrot had been hearing drums and was imitating those sounds. But something in the rhythm immediately triggered me. It sounded like the parrot had been hearing some pretty complex rhythms, it sounded to me like it was switching between straight and triplet time in every bar. (In non technical terms, within four counts it would constantly switch between two completely different rhythmical feels.) When I heard this and realised what kind of opportunities this complexity could give, I immediately ran upstairs to my attic studio and tried imitating / reproducing the groove that I thought the parrot must have heard and was imitating / reproducing.

The triplet feel has something very non-european to it, I’ve been into exploring different takes on rhythm a lot. I’ve been cratedigging on Bandcamp for South American club music, and also been listening to African pop and club music quite a lot. As with every obsessive listening period I go through, it’s only a matter of time before this really starts translating in my output. The same influences are very clearly audible in my ‘Ugly’ remix for Big Dope P and Mighty Mark, I think. ‘Higher’ goes a bit further in rhythmical complexity than where I left off with ‘Ugly’. But as always, my goal with club music is not to make something that sounds complex. The complexity in the groove and the sound has to come across intuitive and immediate, that’s always been the goal, both with Noisia and in my solo work.

I started it in the attic studio upstairs in my house. Then I worked on it in LA from my covid isolation room, because I wanted to play a more finished version at my Brownies and Lemonade show, which was recorded and an early version of Higher appears around the 25 minute mark: https://soundcloud.com/iamthys/thys-brownies-and-lemonade. I mixed the tune in the studio, and then worked on it in airplanes (thank god for noise cancelling headphones!) and hotels travelling to shows and holiday destinations. I finished the track in a full-on heatwave, on a laptop and headphones, in swimwear with a fan pointed at me, while on vacation in Italy :D It’s got quite a story, this one!

Always an unexpected journey that keeps you on your toes to how it all unfolds, yet you never quite reach an ending. Terrifying, but exhilarating all at once, leaving you no choice but to hang on for dear life or let go and enjoy the ride.

Real love is rare to come by, so I savor every moment and take each experience as a blessing. These are the moments that make our lives sweeter. On the week of February 6th, I was set to experience some of the most emotional moments of my life and I had no clue. Moments that would seem regular to someone else. These were good emotional moments on the way, of course.

On Thursday, February 10th I would release my Genesis NFT alongside some friends (virtually). A special moment for me because I truly enjoy my tribe and doing great things with them. These aren’t people I just release music with. These are close friends who I love and care for deeply.  We brought our lifestyle of intentional community to the Blockchain.

On Friday, February 11th I would celebrate my Birthday with my close family. Me, my mother, my wife, my sister, and her boyfriend all went out to eat at one of my favorite restaurants. Dinner was great but the conversation and laughter was food for the soul.

On Saturday, February 12th I would celebrate my Birthday with my close friends. We played games, drank, ate good and just enjoyed each other’s company. During our time, my wife called for a toast to acknowledge me. I didn’t have many words…which is different for me in moments like those. Just, “thank you all for coming through. I love you all, salud!” I went to bed late that night not only warm and tipsy but my soul’s cup was filled to the brim.

That week is what birthed me writing and producing this song. All the moments I described may be normal to other people, especially on the week of one’s birthday. But I felt the love on such a DEEPER level than ever before because of my healing experience.

All the healing I had been doing allowed my cup to be overflowed with a level of love I never felt before.

records.title: Myōken
records.note:
"Myōken" is the Pole Star - that guiding light which, in ancient Japan, was the focus of a Taoist movement in the 7th Century. I love the idea of mythical and folkloric symbolism tied to creative expression and narrative - the idea of old stories being one with futurist stories and using the wisdom of all that to guide us as we venture into a new reality...

This instrumental broken-beat track dips into so many things I love - freeform harmony, piano and synths painting the introspective opening - the Pole Star shining bright and universal... then the intro music gets resampled and flipped as we sidestep into the samples n beats world of my early 00's London underground club years - the urgency and intention of machine-gridded rhythms juxtaposed with the resampled organics of the intro. 

When it comes to tribalism in music, Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti is a perennial inspiration and I wanted to bring some of his vibes into the mix, writing a Fela-influenced melody hook and topping it off with breakbeats and jazz improvisations on the rhodes, bringing us full circle to all the things I love to blend... soulful harmony, syncopated rhythm and free-wheeling improvisation - the jazz soundclashed with something for the dancer's dancer.

my favorite song i’ve ever made.

it was an unexciting saturday morning in my south florida suburb. i’d spent the majority of my life moving around but this specific street had been around for enough years to start to feel like home. if you’d had live footage of my street at 6:00 am, you’d see a series of peaceful front lawns and one with a flurry of movement. a little guy (me) excitedly shoving every last household item into my car as i prepped myself for the 14 hour drive to nashville.

months before, i received what i had interpreted as a series of divine signs to take a chance on myself. i’d saved up some money that i hoped would sustain me for the following year. i was going to go after music full time for the first time ever.

i’d arranged to stay in a friend’s spare bedroom for cheap. my plan was to deliver food a few hours each day and work on music the rest of the time.

i promised my parents that if i didn’t make it big in a year, i’d move back home and take up my career as an airline pilot that i’d put on hold for music. i didn’t think i’d have to, i’d always believed so deeply in my ability to make shit shake. 


the next 12 months were some of the most blissful and painful months of my life.

the best moments: i made music with people i’d looked up to for years, made huge strides towards finding an audience, and found a new community in web3.

the worst moments: a lot of shame, feeling like i’d disappointed the people closest to me, spending nights paralyzed unable to figure out my next steps.

on month 11, i was processing the impending reality that despite all my progress and work i wouldn’t be able to make my 1 year deadline. 

i had to readjust.

records.title: If I Could Say
records.note:
Hi, I’m Kacy Hill. I’m from Phoenix, AZ, now based in Los Angeles. 

Back in 2014, I signed to G.O.O.D. Music and released my debut album, “Like A Woman” three years later.  While I’m thankful for the crash course in the inner workings of the industry my major label experience gave me, I ultimately wanted out (badly). After almost a year of quite literally following Kanye West around to try and get a meeting, I was finally dropped and have been releasing music independently since 2018.

With each of my subsequent album releases I have experimented more with production and the amount of freedom I give myself to make mistakes. In my second album “Is It Selfish If We Talk About Me Again”, I was able to dictate the sounds I heard in my head to collaborators, though rarely sitting down at the computer to dig into the engineering of those sounds. My most recent album, “Simple, Sweet, and Smiling”, was a window into engineering and producing my own music, partially fueled by lockdowns and the inability to actually collaborate in person. 

“If I Could Say” is the first song I’m putting out into the world that I’ve produced and written (and played saxophone on!) entirely on my own. I’m less focused on perfection these days and more interested in what feels most fun and fulfilling to me. I love making music and at this point in life, I pursue whatever will allow me to keep loving the process.

this song is drunk and high on our love for music. our feelings about genres are like our feelings about borders - the more fluid the better. if fela kuti and paul mccartney had a baby that grew up in mexico listening to hip hop, maybe it would sound like this. 

we hope you like it. 

to make this more fun, the first 10 people in the audience will be airdropped a 2nd song/visual NFT, which on top of being a sexy lil song will also function as a ticket to our "welcome tu las californias" show in tijuana on november 4th. cross border x web3. la baja pa'rriba ;)

records.title: Sandman
records.note:
I was born and raised on a farm in Candelo, Australia, about seven hours from Sydney. I’ve lived in the states for the past ten years making and releasing music whilst performing around the world. In 2017 I decided to take a break from the industry, since then I have grown as a producer, and my artistic style has changed. Being off the road gave me time to focus on creating again and I honed in on a new goal of learning to sing. Singing has completely changed the way I think about and create music, I am incredibly excited to share this new journey with you all! 
 
This new era begins with my first new single, “Sandman.” The song slowly came to life over a four-year period, adding all the elements bit by bit to finally create the full track using an array of vintage synths and a live drum kit. I was influenced by rock & roll music at this time so wanted to give the song a more aggressive edge, filled with a huge bass line and melodic leads to create the full experience! With the lyrical meaning of the song I prefer you to take away your own interpretation as that's truly what art is. But if I had to describe it in one word it would be unification!
 
Over the past few years, the industry landscape has changed drastically. Even so, no shift has been more compelling than the power of the NFT community and web3. Being new to the NFT community, this is something that I’m really excited about! There is no better time to enter the community than on the heels of new music, it feels like the perfect storm!

records.title: ILOVEDUILOVEDUILOVEDU
records.note:
hi. i’m sad alex. i’m from delaware, which is a real place other than that wayne’s world line. i have been doing music since i was a very small human and professionally in both nashville and la for the last 9 years. 

i think my biggest strength and weakness in this industry has been my versatility. i can wake up one day wanting to write a sad introspective folk song about my life’s failures, and the next day i write a song about my tits (for real, you can see it on my tiktok and dsps, it did quite well). this makes me a valuable writer and producer in the room for other projects, but can often make decisions about my own the most difficult. because that would require defining the hardest question of all for me, “who am i?” 

but occasionally i make a song baby that defies all that doubt. it flows out effortlessly, i don’t follow any rulebook or try and mold it into something it isn’t. and as a result, it finally feels fully me. it was a no brainer for my genesis sound release to give you one of these precious bbs. this one is partly about a guy that i have written probably 200 songs about, one of those beautifully catastrophic heartbreaks that turns you into an endless bubbling well of emotion. if you haven’t had one of these, i 10/10 recommend for your full experience as a human. but the majority part is about how when you hold onto someone that tightly, after they’re gone it can be hard to figure out where to put that love. the manic titling of this song represents that little voice inside screaming the bitter tired truth that for me, it’s unfortunately often easier to love someone else than to learn to love myself. something i’m working on, shoutout free kaiser therapy. 

i’m very grateful for my experience in the industry the last few years, that same aforementioned epic heartbreak ended up getting me a pub deal and record deal, and as a result i’ve had the opportunity to work with some incredible people, had many cool and fun times, etc. however a few months ago (by choice) i left both in an effort to build the career i want from the ground up. this is my first solo release since leaving my deal, which i wrote and produced fully myself. i’m so excited to connect with all of you and share what i have planned for the future. it is some of the best music and art i’ve ever made, which by saying that i guess means i AM in fact learning to love myself a little bit more xx

records.title: ASSASSIN
records.note:
Remember that thing you couldn’t free yourself from? The habit, the relationship, the mindset. The one that you know will crush you if you stay in any longer.. this is Assassin.

Shortly after signing our deal with the new venture between Mark Hoppus, Pete Wentz, and Sherry Saeedi called Verswire we began a month long stint of writing sessions geared toward creating new music for our next project so we could come out of the gates swinging. In these sessions Assassin was born.

Assassin came from a session with a writing and production group called the Four Horsemen (Aerosmith, Ozzy Osbourn, Highly Suspect, Carrie Underwood, Buckcherry, Kelly Clarkson, etc.)

Going into the process, we said our goal is “Bieber level hooks with the heaviest guitars you can get” and Assassin was born. It was one of those songs that wrote itself. It felt easy, and that is not always the case. 

When it came time to produce the record we had a roadmap in our heads of how we wanted the sonics to come across. We’ve been practicing getting a song written in entirety before adding any production elements. It’s like our ultimate test to see if the song is good or not… if it can it hold up being playing with just an acoustic guitar then we know it's a good song.

records.title: out of focus
records.note: this song child of mine, called "out of focus", is particularly special because it represented a much-needed return to form for me at a very difficult time. music creators can probably relate to the idea that your creative process evolves drastically as you become deeper enveloped by the industry. although i can stay busy with sessions every day sometimes weeks will go by and i'll realize i haven't touched a piano once. songwriting was born as a sacred, solo activity for me: sitting, emoting at the piano, having no idea what i was doing. so although i am grateful that now i can create a song in a multitude of ways, i can start burning out or feeling inexplicably lost if i spend too much time away from the form that brought me to love this expression in the first place. fuel that with a tasty breakup, and this song had everything i needed. i sat, and wrote this top to bottom at the piano, no pre-conceived concept, or melody, or worry if the chorus was "lifting" enough, or if i was being original enough... just did what my instincts wanted to do. i wrote this about feeling pushed away by a person, but as i listen to it now it takes on a new meaning feeling often shoved aside with my career as well. she's truly one of my favorites, and i hope you it makes you feel something🤍

records.title: No Landing
records.note:
The Initial idea for “No Landing” started with a grungy bass line made on an old vintage Memorymoog. This bass line sparked my creative energy, and I started to build out the track with drums, synths and continued expanding on that initial bass line. I arrived at a sound that seemed simple, but still sounded crisp and full-toned. The track was pure, so I didn’t feel it needed to be overcomplicated and oversaturated with wasteful production. To the ear, the elements of “No Landing” are stripped back, which helps encapsulate the energy I wanted the song to exude. 

This single started with production, and I eased into the lyrics, letting the smooth gliding beat serve as the track’s core concept–never forcing a single word. Ultimately, this track has a sonic, unhurried sound that makes listeners feel like they’re floating, never worrying about landing back on the ground.

records.title: Crypto Boy
records.note:
“Crypto ₿oy” is a wake-up call for all the chart-watchers, candle-counters, and JPEG-flippers that find a way to bring crypto into any conversation, no matter what it’s about.

We all know them — checking OpenSea like it’s instagram, obsessing over prices, hodling this, shorting that and unable to focus on anything except Discord.

As exciting as crypto is, and as likely as it is to revolutionize finance in the coming years, I want to shift our attention to a very urgent issue, which is the possibility of SCOTUS overturning Roe v Wade. This attack on reproductive rights is something we should be talking about as loudly as a crypto boy talks about NFTs*. It’s imperative that we band together and fight to protect our fundamental rights. To help bring this together I partnered with Nadya Tolokonnikova of Pussy Riot, who I love and respect, to create the custom art for this NFT.

100% of the proceeds of the sale of this NFT will be donated to The Center for Reproductive Rights (https://reproductiverights.org), a legal nonprofit that is able to accept donations in cryptocurrency.

records.title: YEAHYEAHYEAHYEAH...
records.note:
Welp... 
This songs inception came after an evening that could have been written into a coming of age Shakespeare dramedy.
Sparknotes version... 
Finding a love interest canoodling with a friend.. in your own house... only to turn around and say, it's you they're really interested in... 
The confusion!!

The beat for YEAHYEAHYEAHYEAH... was actually conjured up over 6 months prior to it being written while living in the old Hollywood home of famed director Orson Welles (Citizen Kane), and Frank Sinatra among other notorious names.
After our aforementioned incident.. the beat was pulled up again, and the lyrics "you make me depressed" were penned giving the original demo the title "DEPRESSED" before renaming it to "YEAHYEAHYEAHYEAH..." for the album release.

records.title: FRESH AIR
records.note:
The Body Talks. Picture yourself walking through a crowd of people with a group of friends and hearing the most outlandish bids being called out like an auction. Primitive energy coming at you like hot breath inquiries on a loop. Dysregulated emotions brewing up in your space. A reflection of disunity within your mind,body,and environment. I feel at that point you’d be wanting some fresh air.  After 2020 I really missed dancing out in the city of Miami where I grew up, after being isolated for so long it felt foreign to be out. Reminiscing on my friends and I dressing up to impress ourselves to be quite honest, stepping into a party but by the time we’d arrive I am thinking “I should’ve done a few more reps at the gym” because I am now the protector of the group. The token masc femme needing to step in to interrupt that hungry energy for some peace just to dance freely and safely. Sheesh!

Fresh Air is like a nightlife manual I wrote,  a mantra to repeat before heading out for the night. It is quite comical preparing for a reaction from people when they get rejected. Feels like these days physiologically people are on a clock out here ready to tie something down for the moment. Anxiety and anticipation combined is a rude cocktail before the night out.
Call this song the energy protector! There are ways to respectfully approach the person you want to dance with.
On the contrary - there is something mysterious about non verbal connection and there’s nothing wrong with attention. I feel the most empowered when I am dancing and in my body so there’s this push and pull you’ll here in the song even melodically. The words “Back it up” I have heard in so many songs growing up so I decided to give it multiple meanings. Back it up, meaning Back up so I can Back it up. Also, make room so my shawtys can comfortably back it up on me as well. Ha! It was a lot of fun creating this with Jesse Boykins III with us both growing up in Miami. He fully understood the assignment sonically and morally! I am here to bring awareness to our 5 foot body with audio visual experiences. I have always been intrigued by the conversation between the brain and its podium. So, whether you’re at the gym or going out whatever city you are in allow your body to speak and enjoy the moment.

records.title: BODED
records.note:
Summer of ‘21, Bordeaux, France. It rained, it rained, the sky and I didn’t stop crying. Today I call it cleansing, but back then I couldn’t even call it. My love at the time couldn’t call me either - he was slipping through my fingers by the day. Our relationship slowly died like a campfire that gets smaller while everyone sits around and watches the flames go down, quietly observing. As life would have it, the more we died, the more myself and my music came alive. A whole world opened at the expense of the demise of what I thought was my whole world.

I have good and bad news about heartbreak. The bad news is that it sucks. The good news is that in such deep waters, you can be nothing but honest. The urge to reclaim my identity washed over me and I decided it was time to bring every part of my being to life. With the love & support of my wonderful friends and producers Dean Woodson, Jean Castel, and Edouard Algayon, every sound, language, culture, flavor that makes up my DNA found its way to my fingertips and Boded was born. 

BODED (pronounced Bodèd), Hebrew for LONELY, sings the pain of the man I loved slipping away from me. His body was there, but his heart and spirit were no longer around. “BODED, wanted alive not dead.” When I lost him, I found myself and my sound. This song is a concoction of dying love, living beauty, the Israeli music I was raised on, many languages, few words, all united in harmony between the creaking walls of a castle in the south of France. I hope you enjoy my he(art) as much as I enjoy giving it to you.

records.title: Tell Me The Truth
records.note:
I started investing and learning about crypto in 2012 and I’ve been fascinated by this world ever since. When NFT’s came around I was super excited because of the communities that started developing online around projects. I was able to team up with an incredible visual artist FEWOCiOUS for my first NFT drop, My Head In Your Hands in early 2021. 

I have always been passionate about visual artists and putting on new talent, an interest that meshes perfectly with NFTs. The My Head In Your Hands drop featured an original drawing, animation and music. The project became the first NFT drop with a musical artist to ever gross over 1 million dollars, something that I am really proud of. Since then, I have continued to advocate for the crypto space and minted the “Until I Come Home” music video as an NFT on emerging platform Glass.xyz in the end of 2021. 

Now I am here on Sound.xyz and I can’t wait to build a community for my fans and collectors. 

“Tell Me The Truth” is the first song I have written since “I Feel Like I’m Drowning” that really stemmed from my most vulnerable honest self. Last year I moved from LA back home to NYC - the city where I wrote my first EP and album. “Tell Me The Truth” was the first song I wrote when I moved back. NYC just has a darker vibe that always leaks into my music when I am producing in the city. This song is definitely the song I am the most proud of on my new album. -  Two Feet

records.title: PNTHR
records.note:
We made this song almost two years ago now. One of us had just exited a long term relationship and was going through it, bad. This was the first song we recorded following that situation. It felt like a message. it wasn't planned. it all just came out, with ease. It was like a "hey, don't feel bad for yourself. fuck her. fuck everybody at that point really. Keep your head up, things are starting to happen with this music shit. Just keep going and getting better, you don't need anybody," type message.

This song just created itself basically. I think it was written in like 10-15 minutes. One of those special pieces that felt like it was made in a blackout. Those only tend to come together when you're going through some serious shit. And then without even realizing it, you're probably coping with it by creating that piece of art.

Little did we know, this was the beginning of what would become our album: 'PAIN MUSEUM'. Unconsciously, this song birthed an entire project. It wasn't until later that we made the correlation, but what we did know at that moment, was that we both were in pain. Under completely different circumstances, the one thing we knew we had in common was pain. We were both simultaneously dealing with depression and anxiety, for different reasons. But the glue that kept everything together was the fact that we were hurting together.

Pain became a central theme around all the new material we were creating, and then one day everything clicked. We're building an album. We're building a museum. And we have to credit "PNTHR" for giving birth to this entire concept and credit to the circumstances we dealt with for birthing this universe. We've nearly lost our minds on multiple occasions while building this museum, but it's finally yours on May 13th. No better way to open the museum, than with the exhibit that started it.

records.title: AIRPORT BEERS
records.note:
Hi I’m Cameron and this will be my first release in over 6 years. I can’t tell you how grateful I am to sound.xzy for giving me the opportunity to release a song.  About 8 years ago I bought a grand piano from Paul Kostabi in upstate NY. Even though he gave me a deal I emptied my bank account doing so and could barley afford to move it back to Brooklyn. For the next two years I had nothing but that 6’8” conservatorium grand piano, which only fit in the freight elevator by a couple millimeters, a bed and a white shag carpet rug. That piano really altered my life. I think I played it for about 5 hours a day. Eventually I felt like I wasn’t doing the thing justice so craigslisted some piano lessons. My teacher knew I couldn’t read music so I would send him songs I wanted him to learn and teach me every week. Either that or he’d help me re-voice the backward songs I was writing at the time. Eventually he taught me how to split a chord across octaves, sounds so simple but it really opened my mind to melody and harmony. I started moving chromatically down scales with this newly found technique and let my ears go where they wanted to, if that doesn’t sound too pretentious. That’s where this song was born. It’s been rattling around on my hard drive since then until this year where I had a conversation which free’d me, in way, to let this song happen.     

Airport Beers is about being in flux. The consciousness of transit or a change,  between places or somewhere more metaphysical, creates instability which can be embraced or feared. It depends on whether you’re intrigued by uncertainty or not. Beginnings and endings have always seemed recurring or cyclical to me. Everything in between is never the same. It’s as much about what you do with your time in flux as it is about beer.

records.title: Amazing
records.note:
I’m uber excited to be releasing my new song Amazing on Sound. It’s been a year and some change since I released anything independently. The fact that I get to release it in Web3 is so incredible. I’ve been doing a lot of dope things this year and with this being one of them I’m excited to give you more. There’s a lot of good that’s going on in the music NFT space and I’m so happy to see and be a part of it. I’m honestly glad that I’ll be able to connect directly with my supporters of my art and continue to change lives with my music.

I’m originally from Jacksonville, Florida. I’m a military brat, my dad retired in Florida and me and the rest of family settled there. I couldn’t stay still, so when I graduated high school, I moved to New York City to live my dream of becoming a recording artist. I lived out my dream there for 8 years and right after me and my ex broke up after 5 years together, I decided I needed to move to Los Angeles, California 2020 before the pandemic. I remember this place being one of the stops during the tour I was on back in 2019 with Samoht. I came here   and I can recall saying that LA reminded me of a tall glass of water it was so refreshing and I needed this because I got a chance to take a break from my thoughts.
I’ve been here for two years now and my experience have been  great in so many ways. I finally get a chance to sit with myself and get to know who Devin Tracy is. I’m glad for what New York has taught me and I do miss the food honestly.

The song AMAZING is a beautiful piece about being sexually free. When I wrote this song I was on cloud 9, high as a kite and I didn’t want to come down. Lost in my apartment slightly depressed and still questioning where I was in my life and my relationship with self at the time..I kept smiling at the fact I was beginning to feel free. All I can think about was the night before and the lyrics started flowing. The song is about having intimacy with a person you really like, and you haven’t had that in a while or for others you haven’t had it in that capacity at all. It also speaks about feeling free from judgement and wanting to have that feeling over and over again. That feeling you get where you think can touch God, that feeling you had when you’re on a vacation in Turks and Caicos Island and you dive in the water, and you feel how clean and beautiful it is as you swim to the surface. The adrenalin of you getting on your favorite roller coaster ride and in the beginning, you see the

records.title: Hurt Nobody
records.note:
A year ago I moved back to my country of origin, Georgia. I had been living in the Netherlands for most of my life and felt like I needed to reconnect with home.

A lot happened in the course of a year while being there. I’ve been fortunate enough to spend time with family, make the best music I’ve ever made all while being surrounded by the mountains.

One of the songs I’ve made in this period is “Hurt Nobody”. A song about trying to be righteous in a world that isn’t. A song about honesty. 

This song was set to release on a NFT music platform earlier. It unfortunately didn’t go through because of them being very focused on selling out which went at the expense of the relationship they were building with me. We’re doing it right this time.

records.title: Disaster
records.note:
Hi I’m vaultboy and I’m a singer-songwriter from Jacksonville, FL. I’ve been releasing music for almost 1 year now and put out my debut EP at the start of 2022. The reaction to my music has been insane and I’m stoked at how well it’s been received.  My debut release ‘everything sucks’ had a huge viral moment which helped it spread globally, hitting the #1 spot on the viral charts on Spotify and staying there for several weeks. It even became a western music chart #1 on a major Chinese streaming platform. 

This is my genesis NFT and I’m stoked to be doing it on Sound. I’ve been following the platform and the community for a while now and there’s clearly a lot of awesome trailblazers leading the way in this new Web 3.0 space here. And so so many dope artists that I’m a big fan of who have dropped releases on Sound so I know I’m in good company.

I’m a pretty emotional guy and that seeps into my music and lyrics. ‘Disaster’ is no exception to that. I wrote this song as a part of a songwriting challenge where I try to start and finish a song in 77 minutes. This was the first song of the challenge and I have been surprised to see how much people relate to it! Disaster is about the type of person it hurts to love. Someone who’s problems are often self-inflicted and ends up hurting the people around them: even the people that love them the most. I’m really proud of it, especially as I wrote and produced the song by myself in my home studio. I really hope it resonates with you in someway!

records.title: They Don't Know
records.note:
I made this song at a time in my life where I really feel the world doesn't know. They have no idea what I've been through, and they have no idea what I'm about to do. You see I've been at the top for throughout it all and here to stay, life had crazy plans for me and just as quick as something can go good, it could go bad too, and it went 7 years bad. 

Yeah alot of time has passed since the world has heard from me. A lot has changed too… But not me I’m still the same live wire everybody loves, I’m still smiling ear to ear, and I’m still dancing for the girls making the people laugh. 

No matter what life throws at me I’ll always find a way to smile through it all. Locked away for years in prison didn’t break me… So they tried a little harder and locked me up while being locked up but that didn’t do it either. 

They try to dim your light when they put you in those dungeons. They try to make the time hard, but I knew that one day I’d be free again.

records.title: Hideout
records.note:
I sent out a batch of instrumentals I produced to someone close to me. she said she liked one beat in particular. I had already tried recording to it but wasn't happy with the result. After I spoke with her I decided to have another go at it and made this song to it. 

Hideout is about taking time to yourself and putting your energy towards things that are really important to you. The title of the song also is a nod to the place I'm staying at currently which I refer to as my mountain hideout.

It feels good to be making use of Sound.xyz in a way were I can freely drop whenever I feel like. the artwork for the golden egg is a signed picture taken at the mountain hideout.

records.title: Bad Radio
records.note:
My name is felly.  I’m from Connecticut originally but stay out west in Los Angeles. I found a lane in the music scene a few years ago after years of putting out albums/mixtapes/projects on bandcamp, soundcloud- really whatever was available at the time.  We’re talking 5-6 years ago.  During the golden days of indie platforms I hit a chord in a scene I’m still trying to understand. It is wild to think about how things have evolved since.  

In the early days at school at USC in Los Angeles I helped to form a collective called 2273- named after the dorm room my friends and I would create in.  I kept putting out albums/mixtapes and eventually found myself on multiple nation-wide tours as a headline.  Just my friends and I, selling out large rooms all across the United States.

Fast forward a few years and I’m back living in Los Angeles, after making a pit stop in Brooklyn.  I signed to Sony who I dropped a couple projects with, and then most recently signed with 300 Entertainment.   Throughout this journey of creating the art that speaks true to me and my fans, I’ve met and connected with thousands of people across the US and shared this love for music, life, and we’ve all gotten closer to a feeling of oneness.  I’m filled with gratitude to be a creator and be able to play.  The shows are crazy and my team and I get more inspired to create timeless music by the day.  

Bad Radio is the first single off an invisible project I have that is entirely self-produced.  I say invisible because I’m not sure if it will ever come out, though it contains some of the most personal, true to me songs.  There is no reason for why it won’t come out, but the time for it hasn’t come yet.  I’m thankful to Sound XYZ for providing the first glimpse of this album that the public is able to see.  The songs on this EP are folky, dark, driving.  Very different from the sunny light hip hop sound that I’ve been known to come with.  

To sort of spoil it, the idea behind bad radio is a reflection of how I felt about love at the time.  It’s like, when you hear your favorite song on the radio, but the signal won’t quite come in.  Do you stay there in the static, waiting to hear whatever notes you can make out.  Or do you bash the fucking radio and drive off a cliff?  

The choice is yours.

Young Fel.

records.title: Try to forget it
records.note:
When I started writing songs on bass in 2011 I felt like it gave me some kind of power, I really believe just holding a bass makes you emotionally stronger, you just feel instantly like a badass, the weight of the instrument that you’re holding feels substantial, the depth of the tone, the simplicity in the notes. There’s weirdly so much in that stuff. It’s an incredibly empowering instrument and a useful tool when finding your voice and getting in touch with your feelings. I found a new voice for myself when I started writing on bass, it was writing on bass that led to songs like this. I found it such an important way for me to express myself and lots of the heartache I was going through during my 20s. 

So many songs about bad choices, bad love, bad endings. ‘Try to forget’ feels like the Girl Talk (my 3rd album) era to me. There are still songs from the Girl Talk era coming out of me and still so many locked away in a chamber. It’s a time that was so formative for me, I was dealing with true independence, facing demons, facing bad guys, making bad choices. It felt a bit like Buffy season 5. I felt I was facing the world and was seeing it’s dark underbelly, realising I was an adult but still just a girl underneath. Music has always been the best way for me to deal with my life and this was never more true during this era. I love still being able to access that moment and feeling, it’s youthful, rebellious and angsty, it’s still in my stomach.

‘Try to forget it’ was written in a rehearsal room, there’s a ton of songs written in dingy dark rooms with dirty old amps and microphones, sounds of drums coming through the walls from other bands, cold damp rooms, bad lighting and bad air. I love spending time in these caves and playing for hours, sometimes nothing comes of it but every now and then you catch onto something you’re playing with and it becomes a song, that’s what happened with 'Try to forget it', it was just an afternoon in a rehearsal room jamming on the bass. 

‘Try to forget it’ is a punk love disaster song, written on bass about the car crash you know is coming. In love with someone that doesn’t have respect for you? in love with someone that has hurt you already? You try to forget it, try to make excuses for them and their actions despite knowing better. You make your own bed and you lie in it, you’re aware you should change the sheets, you should probably burn the bed and move house, but you’re not ready. Something is making you stay. Somehow

records.title: NITELITE
records.note:
Hello all,

My name is RIZ LA VIE, and this is my song, NITELITE. I began making this song in Malibu in May 2021, with my long time friend and creative partner Daniel Hartzog. I had brought Dan with me to Malibu after a shared traumatic loss of a friend, to create, swim, and heal, together. Out upon the hillside in Malibu, during our first weeks there, overlooking the expanse of ocean, we would see a giant full moon rise every night. A spectacle. My love of the moon is certainly not new but these felt like special views. I wrote the song about all things celestial, captivating, and endearing, the moon being the mascot of those qualities to me, and the chances of experiencing these qualities at all. I wrote about how, like a partner with an empathetic ear may hear out the woes of their loved ones from time to time, and may even occasionally lend guidance, the moon will listen like you are the only two in the universe, and how, like many instances in this life, if you take a moment to listen to it and give it the space to communicate, it just may reflect something you need to hear.

We continued working on NITELITE and the album at Dimension 70 Studios in NYC’s lower east side throughout June 2021, recording some sections just a couple days after broken collarbone surgery. It's a song that has always existed through and because of healing, support, and a bit of help from the cosmos. With a fresh coat of paint bringing it into 2022 and beyond, one of the guiding lights of my debut album is ready to see the light of day, and we’re very excited to present it to you all. 

Space therapy,  cosmic prayer, or shouting to the heavens, Nitelite is for moonlight lovers, chill thrill-seekers, and web3 natives. Y'all are amazing thanks for being an active part of this. If you ever need to yell something into the night sky, and don’t know what to say, don’t hesitate to use these words.

records.title: Wonderland
records.note:
I'm very excited to be premiering my newest song Wonderland here on Sound. I think the premise of the lyrics and the sonics lend themselves very well to this new wonderland that is Web3. Being an independent artist coming up in this new age of technology, there are so many middlemen that stand between you and your potential fanbase and I'm so happy that I'm getting the opportunity to connect directly with supporters of art and lovers of music alike

I was born in Inglewood California and spent half of my childhood in Cali, and then my parents moved my brothers and me out to Louisiana where I finished high school. music for me has always been an escape from the world around me, and an outlet for a lot of internal conflicts I hadn’t yet learned to articulate as a kid. The day I picked up a guitar I felt something change inside me, it was a change that gave me hope in knowing there was something out there that could quell even the most vicious storms that were going on in my heart and in my life around me. 

Wonderland feels like a peaceful escape from reality, but the lyrics are a cry out to the world about mans (hu-man) relationship with themselves, and with the environment around them. I talk about how some people view a tree as a source of shelter or kindling to be burned for warmth, while others may view a tree as a living being and as a source of the very air we breathe. Now we all need shelter, but having an understanding and respect for nature is paramount because the earth can only give us exactly what we need. Any more than that throws the world out of balance, a lot of us live lives of excess without thinking about how every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Whether you look at things from a yin-yang perspective, or you view things like Newton, it's the same concept. 

I hope that this song brings people peace, even if for a few minutes and shows us that stillness and reflection are important for growth - we must be focused more on the natural progressions of life rather than the constant production of goods and services. Community is the only way forward in my mind and heart, and I am grateful to be a part of this community full of pioneers blazing a new path into the future! 

Peace 
~ Brandon ~

records.title: dopamine
records.note: Hey I'm dwilly - I’m a pop/electronic artist from the southern town Greenville, South Carolina. After my last EP, I took a break from releasing music through a major label and now I'm hyped to enter the web3 space and release my first NFT independently.  Most people know my music as eclectic and synth driven. I wrote, produced, and sang this 100%. My musical roots stem from classical music to classic rock to Rebecca Black. This is the first song I have released since covid and it's about shaking off negative feelings and just vibing bro- amirite lmao. "dopamine" is a new direction for the dwilly project that has given me creative freedom as an independent artist. To all my fans- I hope you enjoy it as much as I enjoyed creating it.

records.title: WISHFUL THINKING
records.note:
I’m grentperez and I’m a 20 year old artist from Western Sydney, Australia. My music is heavily inspired by a lot of the music I listened to growing up such as, The Eagles, Bread, Musiq Soulchild and Frank Ocean

I released my first demo music in summer of 2020, moving into official releases throughout 2021 and since then my music has been reaching audiences all around the world and I’m currently undergoing my first tour ever.

This record ‘Wishful Thinking’ is about a relationship that’s yet to be, to daydream a lifetime's worth of love from the first moment you met that special someone. I thought of this song as if I lived in a world where I didn’t ask my current partner out, how I’d probably spend my days wandering around. This song was also heavily influenced by cheesy 2000s movies, such as ‘13 going on 30 / suddenly 30.

records.title: Beautiful Place
records.note:
I very rarely use my highest range so it was fun creating this layered sounds and playing in the sky vocally. I mostly wanted it to feel like morning meditation. A song a person could listen to no mater how difficult the moment and recenter themselves. And I used a lot of vocal restraint and didn’t sing like it was time for alter call because I really want the listener to sing along as personal affirmation that beauty is all around and in them.
