Love YahZarah

records.title: MIDNIGHT FT. MAGSY
records.note:
Making music has always been such a heavily personal thing for me. I started as a kid in Chicago just making beats in my bedroom at my parents house then met the Louis The Child guys, they were coming up at the same time as me, and we got a studio together and that really helped me get a foot in the door in the EDM scene. I wasn’t sure if the music thing was for real until I saw on Twitter that this DJ group Zeds Dead played one of my songs on a massive stage at a huge festival which blew my mind because it was a song I made in my bedroom at my parents house. That made me feel like maybe I could really do this for a living and that’s kind of when I became super committed to the whole thing. Working on whatever projects I or the Louis guys had going on in the same studio really drove us to level each other up, it was pretty foundational for me and it’s probably the reason why I like to evolve my sound so much. I like blending genres or artists that might not seem like they’d make sense together which is kind of what I’m trying to do with this new project coming out. 

I want to continue this trend of pushing myself to evolve musically so working with Sound.xyz for this new track Midnight Blue is actually super exciting. I think it would be pretty dumb not to explore web3 and the NFT scene, I think it’s the future of the industry. Midnight Blue is the perfect track to debut with as well because it really showcases that unique and unexpected genre-blend that I try to constantly push the limits of. On top of that, I also play with rhythm and tempo a little more towards the end of the track which is something that I want to start to showcase a little more because it just adds one more element to the mix. This is a first for me so I’m really stoked to see how the track fits into Sound.xyz's platform–I think folding NFTs into the music industry opens up a lot of possibilities for artists too, so overall I'm really excited to work with them.

records.title: Ego
records.note:
I wrote Ego in a writing session with Dan Henig and Linden Jay who both worked with me on Cherry Wine.  I think this is their first times being involved in an NFT so I'm stoked that I can help bring some fellow creators into the web 3.0 space with me on this journey. 

I hope that I'm going to extend my collector-base with this release and welcome more NFT collectors into my community.  I'm about to be doing lots of touring all over the place and so I'm hoping that I'll be able to connect with collectors in different cities around the world, that would be so cool.

records.title: Got It
records.note:
Since I released my first EP in 2016 I’ve realized that making full length projects is a really important fuel to my creativity. Also the feeling of freedom and a fresh start I get after putting out a project I have worked on for a long time. It allows a period of mindless producing that eventually finds a direction and purpose that often and hopefully results in a project that’s very different from the previous. 

As I’ve gotten older (now 26) I’ve become more aware of how I get drawn to certain palettes over periods of time and how I can use this to make more cohesive projects. Thinking more conceptual with my sound choices and moods gives me a bigger feeling of purpose when making music. 

“Got It” is a result of the last couple years where I’ve been drawn towards medieval sounding things. Harpsichords, worn instruments, simple, folky (no pun) sounding music. It’s the first single from my upcoming project “Castle Tapes” and it captures a lot of the palette that has been inspiring me the last couple years. Hope you enjoy it! Cheers!

records.title: Dip
records.note:
My musical journey started in 2014 after I put up my first edit on Soundcloud by recommendation from a friend. I was surprised at the interest it got and fast-forwarding one year I signed a record deal and moved out to Los Angeles. Here I met a lot of like-minded producers and I started playing shows on tour with Louis The Child and Whethan.

After a few years of touring my interest shifted more towards producing for others and I’ve had a lot of fun in that realm. I got the opportunity to work with some amazing artists including BØRNS, Tove Lo, Carly Rae Jepsen and Anna of the North to name a few. It's always been important to me to dive into new things, and this was a meaningful step in my musical path.

In late November last year I tore my meniscus and had to go through surgery. I stayed mostly in bed for over a month straight and felt this incredible dread from not being able to do the things I normally do. Music became the best therapy during that period and I started making loads of beats. It was a really fun and creative path for my music, which I hope shines through in this track.

This is the result of being limited to headphones and a computer. I hope you enjoy <3

records.title: Stick and Move
records.note:
When making the music I love, I tend to keep my head down, and the volume up as music keeps me going. Music has played a significant role in my life, being my primary form of therapy. I was very insecure, introverted, and struggled with social anxiety as a kid. I still, to this day, enjoy my alone time much more than going out with others, but I no longer struggle the way that I used to because of music. 

As always, there comes a time when you have to look up and step out to take yourself to the next level. In doing so, you often receive a lot of pushback from people around you who don't agree with or understand your vision. This is entirely normal and expected when you're doing something great. One thing I personally didn't expect was for others' insecurities and traumas to get in the way of their support for what I do. I recall being very insecure in myself and my craft at one point, and as a result, I studied those that I felt were much better than me. This never made me not want to support what they were doing; It only attracted me more. As I venture deeper into the music industry, I notice that some people will know who you are and what you do but choose to ignore you because they don't want their shine taken away. This song offers a form of support while also addressing the issue at hand so that we can continue to grow as artists.

The song gives off a fun and groovy vibe to represent my understanding of dancing. I compare the issue to dancing because that's exactly what it is, a rhythmic (repeated) sequence of steps taken by multiple parties resulting in the form of entertainment. While the matter can be entertaining, the main focus is the conflict that can arise between both parties if they are not on the same rhythm. Insert the title, "Stick and Move," a boxing technique that I consider a dance representing the conflict between both parties. 

In the first verse, I express my interaction with some of these individuals who have slighted me in ways they may not have noticed and how it made me feel. Though it can get to me at times, I tend to be very forgiving and understanding which keeps my confidence up, igniting the fire within. The second verse goes deeper into the issue, explaining my thought process on understanding what's really happening and how to solve it. Ultimately we all need a little patience. Even when frustrations are high, the conversation can still be had in healthy ways so that we all can thrive and flourish within this industry.

records.title: Forgive 2 Forget
records.note:
Wassup my name is Alann8h im half thai half canadian and I like to sing or whatever. 

I went to LA around March 2022 for the first time after wanting to go forever. This was at one of my first ever live, in-person studio sessions so it was a pretty crazy and nerve-wracking experience. apob asked me what I wanted to do and all I had was this idea of a funky bass line so we built the whole song up from there and everything flowed so easily and came out so perfectly. We continued adding on layers of different instruments and different melodies to get to how the song is now as well as lyrics and vocals. It was a very interesting experience finally being able to work with somebody other than just me in my bedroom and it taught me a lot about opening my mind and exploring new ideas and things which really played in a lot with the meaning of the song just looking into the future. It was so great to see and work with like-minded individuals and someone as talented as apob. It gave me this new sense of wonder and new perspective on what I can do. As an independent artist, I’ve always looked to find ways to support and fund my creativity without having to sign to a label. I’ve been lucky to get some early traction on Spotify and stuff which isn’t really something I had ever planned for but from that came the labels asking me to sign. Before web3 I didn’t think there was another way I could bring my visions to life without the stability a label can provide. Platforms like sound are giving artists like me a chance to fund our art, empower the fans and create a community of people with the same ethos that artists deserve better. 

The indie-pop tune was produced by apob and written and sung by alann8h. It's an uplifting song about learning to forgive and forget the past in order to continue on to the future and that whole moment of realization. It's about letting go of everything and not holding onto negativity and things that you cannot change. Succumbing to that realization in order to continue on in life.

records.title: nvm
records.note: “nvm” is a song that was a catalyst for a pivotal change in my life. I was in nashville on a trip to write with my one of my nearest & dearest collaborators Chris Wallace & I was telling him how something deep within me was churning & calling for change & it felt like it was time for me to leave my home & everything that I’ve ever know to find something different out of life. Perhaps not only of intrigue and palpable vibrancy, but one more thing to challenge my comfort zone and see what that would elicit in me musically. We wrote & produced the skeleton of the song within an hour & finished it the next day. I spent that week with him in Nashville writing songs & exploring the city & when I got back to LA I immediately told my friends & family that I was trading the glitz & glamour of Hollywood to hopefully find peace, tranquility & renewed inspiration in Nashville. The boxes on the cover art are the actual boxes I then used to pack up all of my things. Very symbolic for me. Music has always been an intuitive way of bringing forth & expressing my my soul’s language. Music has a funny way of letting you speak your truest words before u may even consciously know them. “nvm” did that for me & will forever be an incredibly special song in my career for that reason. I hope you enjoy it & who knows, i hope maybe it can inspire one of you to do something you’ve always been scared of, but longing to do<3

records.title: Good Morning
records.note:

records.title: Let Go

x sim

records.title: Oh Well
records.note: There was no more sun, no more wind, no more people.  So agent C boarded her ship and went up. Up and up and up past the disease and the filth and the orange clouds so thick with guilt that they held her and cried as she barely pierced their fat. When she reached the black of space a weight was lifted and she wept.  Looking down at earth one final time, C decided that her home was no longer her home but a cabin in the woods of regret.  Somewhere far away a space port called to her and begged for her to arrive.  The silence sounded like rage, but the weapon would be ready when she awoke from her 30 year slumber. 432 days into the sleep she would dream again and she prayed for a good dream.   This is her dream, this is our dream… the danger is big but we’d rather have a broken skull than a broken heart. One day we will be there, until that day we will think only about being there.

records.title: Kiss Me Like I'm Drowning
records.note:
I am a 23 year-old independent artist from a small town in South Africa. An atypical, non-traditional mixed kid, taking up space in Web3 to revolutionize the music industry. 

I am…
KAIEN CRUZ.

MY STORY
I released my very first song, after my older sister heard me singing in my bedroom and eagerly dragged me to the studio. No one really knew I could sing or play guitar, until the song ended up on the radio. It quickly began topping the charts & getting nominated for awards. A couple of months later, I sang at my second live performance ever in front of 90,000 people opening up for Justin Bieber’s Purpose Tour.
Fast forward, I moved to LA just before the pandemic & have since released two EP’s, ‘Demos For Ransom’ & ‘BUFFERING…’, got signed to CAA, went on my first US Tour and have been booked to perform at major stages including Governor’s Ball in NYC & SXSW in Austin.


WHY WEB3
Growing up queer in a small town meant it was always easier to talk to people online that I could relate to. Platforms like tumblr played a big role in cultivating a space & community, where I could connect with like-minded people. I have found this same sense of connectivity & community in Web3.
After the success of my independently funded & pushed EP, I went on multiple different label runs, meeting execs from every major label. I quickly realized that a lot of people in the music industry didn’t understand the vision of what I was trying to create, not allowing me to have full creative control and reins on my future. Technology, music & entertainment go hand- in-hand, so naturally, I have a big interest in creating a community on Web3 that can be a part of my journey & career as an artist, while simultaneously creating a blueprint for aspiring artists that want to retain creative control as well.
I want to encourage others to stop fighting for a seat at a table that was never built for them and instead create their own table, specially curated to their needs, interests and passions!

'Kiss Me Like I'm Drowning' is a cinematic sound journey of self-discovery and exploration. I hope you enjoy!

records.title: Finish Line
records.note:
Every one of us has a race that we have to run. For some of us, this race is chosen. For others, we’re thrown into the storm of competition without knowing what the hell’s going on.  Where I’m from, the popular race to run is the race for fame. Folks from around the globe come to Los Angeles to follow their dreams, always with images of grandeur to fuel the pursuit of the seemingly impossible.

While it’s easy to get caught up in the noise of it all, I’ve managed to sort out a lot of the struggles with being an artist by struggling with my friends. From the moment I left home to pursue this, I knew it would be hard fought to do it without some homies by my side. From my hometown, to SoundCloud, and now with a family in web3, I’ve been lucky enough to have carved out a temporary place for my friends and I in this ever-changing ecosystem we call “the Music Industry”. It took quite a while, but one of the clearest lessons we’ve taken from our experiences is this: there is no "Finish Line". There is no particular point where you should stop. It’s a matter of choosing a direction, and sticking to your guns. The raceway will reveal itself as you go, but only if you decide to take a second to look back. I’ll continue to press my mind until the wheels fall off, as it’s been an honor to have gotten this far in the race in the first place.

records.title: Would You Like It
records.note: This song means so much to us we want you to have it for free. It's inviting and lush and metallic and purple. Like Androids eating cotton candy, like taking a warm bath on a space ship. The computer winks back. When we had to meet on zoom to make this music something just clicked. True collaboration, no thought, no fear, too bad music isn't always this free. Our only request, is when u listen for the first time, close your eyes. We love you.

records.title: alone at last
records.note:
ah, alone at last. 

i have trouble when there’s too much noise; i get pretty quickly exhausted around others. i appreciate company, but too much time spent without quiet starts to nag at me.

“alone at last” is an acknowledgment to these feelings i have which i know aren’t always healthy but make up who i am. i value my friends, and i value solitude. i don’t always want to be alone, but usually i do.

records.title: TESTING
records.note: So... the last time I was here, I was trying to convince myself that I wasn't done working towards the "Finish Line". Thanks to the awesome supporters and engineers here at sound.xyz, we sold out instantly. Since then, I've been stretching between attempting to maintain relationships with extremely talented friends, working on heds.app, and generally keeping my head as down as possible. More recently, I've started to explore what it means to be a creative. When you start out your career with absolutely zero sense of infrastructure and a job title that doesn't exist yet, it's easy to feel overwhelmed by the stress of simply trying to survive. After 15 years of linking & building, many of my friends in the creative field struggle to find a tangible direction for them to go. I'm here to argue: there really is none. Winging it is truly the answer. Out of every decision in the creation of a record, the most exciting to me are still those "happy accidents". A knob slightly tweaked can add so much emotion, changing the direction of your process completely. That's the beauty in creativity to me. The ability to paint with your decisions, to maximize your creative return in order to create more, to increase your footprint in the culture of your choice. Bob Ross was really onto something.

records.title: Runnin' Back
records.note:
Hey y'all, DLG. here 👋 

(You can call me Dave though, we're homies like that).

I started playing guitar when I was 6. I played classical guitar, with nylon strings. I loved the warmth of the instrument, how I could feel each note resonate in the wood grain against my chest. I spent many years taking lessons and playing in classical guitar recitals, freezing my ass off in a church somewhere on the edge of town. I would wear a black turtleneck and sit up straight as an arrow. 

As time passed, I decided that sometimes I wanted to hunch over when I played the guitar. I wanted to hum along to the notes, play random chords until something stuck, experiment more. I was always very adventurous with the rest of my art (mainly drawing, painting, and origami at the time), so writing my own songs felt like a natural step to take. 

I began to try properly singing when I was about 12. Prior to then, my singing experience was mainly singing along to Cake and The Beatles on road trips. I was angsty and I needed an outlet, so I would sit crosslegged in my living room and belt out whatever lyrics crossed my mind.  Garageband entered the picture a couple years later, and the songs I was writing in my living room (and with my rock band, Fat Boy and The Midnight Snackie) could be immortalized on my hard drive. 

I kept writing songs throughout high school, as well as creating physical art. Drawing, painting, printmaking, origami, and sculpting have always been very important parts of my life, and my music is heavily influenced not just by other musicians, but by painters & illustrators as well. My favorites include Joan Miró, Dalí, Peter Sis, and Chris Van Allsburg. 

Near the end of highschool, I discovered Ableton, and formed a band with my close friend and collaborator Josh Mosier. I eventually explored producing on my own, and began to tinker with an EP during my freshman year of college.

I spent a lot of time during college locked away in my room, in a manic daze, determined to finish songs. I was addicted to getting better. I released songs with no intention of having them heard or being a successful musician; I just needed to get them out there. It was my form of therapy.

For my artist name, I chose DLG., the initials of my last name and the nickname that everyone in college already called me.

One song after another, and I started to get some recognition. Suddenly, the hours locked away in my room didn't seem so crazy. I realized I should take music as seriously

records.title: Crashing
records.note:
"Crashing" is the instrumental of my single "Again" w/ Juliana Chahayed, released Aug. 12th via Friends of Friends. The two songs were released as a double single as the lead for my upcoming EP "Always Less". 

I started on "Crashing" somewhere around a year ago while in the midst of a major identity crisis regarding my music, and abandoned it when I wasn't able to confidently flesh it out. Almost a year later, Juliana and I got in touch, and right away I knew I had the idea for her. I sent her what was then the demo version of "Crashing" and she quickly sent me back a vocal idea which instantly inspired and excited me. There's not a lot of vocalists I connect with or enjoy the sound of, but her voice so flawlessly fit over the instrumental, and I knew that was all that I was missing. 

Once the process began of finishing the song with Juliana's vocals, the instrumental came together much more naturally. Having that inspiration and foundation of the vocal layers really helped me see it through. I'm extremely proud of this instrumental which so vividly conveys the calm essence I wanted to communicate when first beginning the instrumental a year ago.

records.title: CRYSTALLIZED
records.note: CRYSTALLIZED was a song born from isolation and chaos, completed over a week during the summer of 2021 in rural Washington.

records.title: WRONG WAY
records.note:
"Wrong Way" is about being unsure. It's about not knowing if the path you're choosing is the right one, but continuing along it either way. It's about the feeling i get when i have 5 different feelings clashing at once (or something like that). It's like reaching the top of a hill, only to find a greater challenge ahead of you. It's an unexplainable feeling, and i hope the mood of this song will convey it to people. 
I want to be able to express more of my roots musically, and express the things that sit on my mind usually. I'm not good at writing how i feel out, so im hoping this will help. This is such a small piece to the puzzle, but i hope the picture will start to show with a few more pieces coming soon.
What's most important is that i appreciate everyone and anyone that is/ will be apart of this. I can't wait to show whats next.

Hey, I’m Munn. I grew up in Indiana but currently live in Nashville! When I was 15 I started playing guitar and writing music but didn't take it seriously until my Sophomore year of college.
     
In the summer of 2018, leading up to my Sophomore year, my engagement with my fiancée fell through, and I lost all interest in school. I was struggling to heal from the breakup, and I had no idea what I wanted to do with my life. It was during this time that I wrote my first song in over a year called I Tried. To this day, I can't describe how I felt after making that song. I had finally found my way to heal, and, from then on, creating music was all I wanted to do.
     
Around this time, a producer that I had connected with in 2017, named Dylan Stiles, was sending me beats every day. I would write and record to these beats every night using an Xbox headset and GarageBand. As time went on, we both decided that the best thing we could do was to drop out of school and go all-in on music. In July of 2019, with less than 4,000 monthly listeners on Spotify, Dylan and I moved to Nashville to do just that.
     
After a failed EP, we realized I needed a better strategy for putting out music. We decided that the best thing I could do was put out a new song every two weeks until one caught traction. On September 6th, 2019, we released the first song following this plan called I Lost Myself.
     
Currently, I am a fully independent singer/songwriter based out of Nashville. My team and I have been building my fan base over the past couple years and have amassed over a hundred million streams, a million monthly listeners on Spotify, 200k+ subs on YouTube, and more, all independently. While our music hasn’t stopped growing by any means, moving into the NFT space for additional support and a new way to connect with listeners was the logical next step for us.

Before dropping out of college and leaving everything behind for music, I was attending a small college alongside my then-fiancé and many hometown friends. When my engagement fell through, I was crushed, and everything about that town that I once loved became insignificant to me. In fact, I started to hate all of it. I couldn’t bare to be in that place any longer, so I left it all behind; I had to. records.title: sad girls always finish first
records.note:
hi, my name’s alaina castillo. i’m 22 years old from houston, currently living in los angeles. for me, music started in my bedroom in texas when i was by myself either after school, work, or sneaking away when life got stressful. i was in choir throughout my school years, but was always told to focus on my studies and things that would put me on a secure path in life. when i was about to finish highschool, i realized that all i wanted to do was break the cycle and make something for myself. i wanted to make those around me proud so that they could see the dream i had in mind was achievable. to them, not being able to see the end result was an immediate red flag for me to stop, but to me it meant that i could create whatever outcome i wanted. 

i started making covers on youtube, trying different things, & meeting the amazing people who supported me from the start. i still talk to a lot of them to this day & don’t know where i would be now if it weren’t for them supporting me and hyping up each upcoming video. starting with a small community was the part that i remember enjoying most. they saw my first video blow up, my channel start to grow, & eventually my move out to los angeles where i started doing small tours and festival performances. it was something that i had always dreamed of while making videos with just a camera and an instrumental track on my computer. 

when i started releasing music as an artist, there were moments where i thought i had found myself, but always had to ask if it was really me because i had no clue who i was or what i wanted to say. i would find it in lyrics of songs or melodies that made me feel something, but i always felt a disconnect. i didn’t realize until recently that the person i was looking for inside myself was hurt, broken & hiding. expressing myself was never something that came easy and i forced myself to forget my own problems to please the versions of myself that other people had. before the start of 2022, i went back to houston with this new mindset, recorded music in my spare room, & went back to the reason i wanted to start making music. the reason for wanting to desperately create a world that i could escape to. it came from sadness & trauma, regret & emotional abuse, but also from optimism. a desire to do more, achieve more & show people that i could make it because there was nothing that made me feel more like myself than making music.

records.title: Loved By U feat. morgxn
records.note:
Music is a universal language--truly loved by all. Through creating this song, both Morgxn and I were able to find some peace during these tumultuous times.  

The origin story: The introduction actually began at a Halloween party hosted at Charli XCX's home. Fast forward to the pandemic, Morgxn sends me a very special vocal he had written in London just before the lockdown. The message and lyrics resonated so deeply that I had to create a song that truly represented how I felt.

Though the song was written before our society shutdown--it had more meaning during.  This song is about the idea of craving touch that feels euphoric and cathartic. After dealing with 2 years of physical separation from our loved ones, this song is a celebration of togetherness and our love for each other.

records.title: Sober
records.note:
Hello! Superflirt here:) I am a 21-year-old indie-pop/rock artist from Summit, New Jersey. Growing up, I played drums and guitar in rock bands and then shifted to a singer-songwriter sound as I started writing and recording my own music. I’m currently based in San Diego and have been leaning into a nostalgic, upbeat 80’s sound. I love creating music with huge punchy drums, reverberated guitar lines, and layered vocals.

“Sober” is an anthem for that sober friend at a party. When I wrote this I was so over people acting like I owed them an explanation for why I didn’t want to drink. There was a long time that I felt isolated because of this and I wanted to explore that feeling. 

This is the most proud I have been of a song’s sound quality and writing to date. I’m so excited to share it with the world, alongside a music video shot on 65mm film by No Storage Productions. I appreciate those who want to join me on this journey and am especially grateful to be on a platform with so many other talented artists!

records.title: Cwejman
records.note:
My name is Alex aka Boys Noize, DJ & producer from Berlin, Germany. I started to DJ in clubs when I was 16. As a teenager I was working in a house and techno record store, so when I started to make my own music I decided to create my own label to be 100% independent. The music was released through limited presses of vinyl - it was music for DJs only. You were only able to find the music in a select network of house & techno record stores around the world. 

After the first few releases, well known DJs started to play my tracks in their sets, and I suddenly was getting booked both as DJ and to remix the likes of Depeche Mode and Daft Punk (!!). Out of the 100 remixes I’ve done there were indeed some hits, and these propelled me to big stages like Coachella and Glastonbury and studio sessions with A$AP Rocky, Bon Iver, Frank Ocean and Lady Gaga.  It still feels surreal to think about where it all started.

This brings me to my release today. “Cwejman“ is a classic Boys Noize banger - unreleased until now - and it’s a big one in my current DJ sets. The name "Cwejman" comes from one of my modules in my modular system that I've used to create the main sound of this track. 

Bringing limited editions to the digital age gives me the same vibes I had in my early days when I spent all my money on limited vinyl presses. Every DJ knows the feeling of dropping something rare in their sets, something that few others have. Offering DJs that feeling again while supporting artists is the magic of Sound.xyz

records.title: IDK You Yet (Original Demo)
records.note:
Hey I’m Alexander 23 an artist/songwriter/producer from Chicago who lives in LA but still roots for the Bulls. I started making music when I was 9 years old after seeing my dad play guitar. I knew instantly that if I wasn’t gonna make it to the league that I had to make music for the rest of my life. I played in bands in high school and dropped out of college after my freshman year while studying engineering to tour as a drummer/bass player.

I originally moved to LA in 2018 to write/produce songs for other artists. It was cool to start to try to make a living doing in the studio, but I couldn’t help but feel like something was missing. I was working with talented artists, but I wasn’t feeling creatively fulfilled. I called my manager and told him to cancel all of my sessions. I wanted to be an artist and make my own music.  I wanted to exist musically outside the studio.

Fast forward a little bit and I was able to release my first music as Alexander 23 in 2019 and was fortunate enough to go on tour with Omar Apollo and Chelsea Cutler that same year. When the pandemic hit in 2020, everything changed, as it did for everyone. Tour was cut short and I went back to LA feeling defeated. That initial isolation brought me back to a time in my own life when everything was going wrong: personally, professionally, romantically. It was that same feeling that something really important was missing.

This feeling inspired me to write “IDK You Yet” and this song changed my life. This year I was able to go on tour opening for one of my heroes John Mayer, was nominated for a Grammy for co-producing ‘good 4 u’ by Olivia Rodrigo and just last week “IDK You Yet” went platinum (three things that don’t even sound real when I say them outloud). I wanted to share the original demo of  “IDK You Yet” because hearing it in its original stripped form is such a strong reminder of the power of a single song. As fans of music I think we all understand that and it’s what keeps us coming back for more.

records.title: Wild Side
records.note:
Suki Waterhouse catalogs the most intimate, formative, and significant moments of her life through songs. You might recognize her name or her work as singer, songwriter, and actress, but you’ll really get to know the multi-faceted artist through her music. Growing up in London, Suki gravitated towards music’s magnetic pull and always saw the medium as a way of expressing creativity and telling stories. Suki has drawn comparisons to the Paisley Underground sound of Mazzy Star and to the 60s influenced girl group reimagining of bands like Stockholm’s The Concretes and Glasgow’s Camera Obscura.

On “Wild Side,” Suki wonders aloud if her love would return to an ex if they came calling, particularly because the excitement and lust of a prior relationship can be so enticing. Suki sings, “when you got that ex who’s crazy, they’re always running through your mind / remember when we had a wild side?”

“Wild Side is about recognizing each other’s past, the beauty and the fear that comes in reminiscing about who you used to love,'' says Suki about the record.

records.title: RIP You and Me
records.note:
RIP You and Me was one of the first songs I wrote for my debut album Aftershock. Ironically, it ultimately became the clear and obvious choice to be the final song on the album (more on this later). I hadn’t really written any songs since my previous EP “Oh No, Not Again!” and didn’t know exactly where I wanted to go with the next round of music which I think is both the scariest and most freeing time for a songwriter. I booked a spontaneous trip to Miami to get inspired and that’s where this song started.

While I was in Miami, I realized that although a relationship of mine had ended, there was still a lot I wanted to say to her and things I hoped she knew. I began to think of this song as a kind of eulogy for a relationship and that’s where the title was born. After I had the working concept and some of the lyrics I sat down at the piano and that chorus melody line was one of the first things that came out. It was really funny working on this sad piano song while all of the other studios were bumping insanely loud reggaeton. I actually think this weirdly ended up inspiring the bridge, in that I knew the song had to dial up to 10 at some point to really capture the emotion.

When I got back to LA, I lived with the song for a little bit and really loved it, but it felt like something was missing to really put it over the top. It felt like one of the most harmonically sophisticated songs I had ever made and I really wanted to lean into that. I called Charlie Puth and had him not only replay all of the piano I had played but also add that outro solo which I could not be happier to have as the last moment on the album. 

This song had to be the final song on the album because to me this song is closure personified. It’s looking back at all the highs and all the lows, exhaling, and saying ‘we gave it our best shot’. I think of the duality of the really intense bridge and the outro piano solo as kind of the perfect encapsulation of that feeling. I think this song defines the Aftershock era and I’m so grateful for it.

records.title: When I'm With You
records.note:
This song is for several things. It’s for my girlfriend, my family, and my friends for being there for me when we all got stuck inside; for the feeling of being at shows, looking over to the person next to you and knowing you both feel the same thing; and for the nostalgia of times spent together when you’re away.

I’m really excited to be an independent artist for the first time since I was 19. Over the past five years, I’ve put together a catalog that didn’t quite fit in with my major label releases; “When I’m With You” is the first of these. Lately, I’ve built a modular synth, and many of the sounds I’ve been crafting songs around have come together so much more organically. The newer records feel personal and intimate.

After being a supporter and collector of sound.xyz songs since the beginning, I’m stoked to be able to drop this record with them as a series of NFTs. This release will help fund future projects, as well as give the fans a collectible to hold on to. Owning an edition will also provide access to a secret section of the MELVVille Discord.

My official debut EP “Shift In Momentum” will be released later this year. This is the first single from that project. Sit back, space out, and enjoy.

records.title: night dive
records.note:
Almost exactly 3 years ago, in the early spring of 2019, we were beginning to release songs from our debut album, komorebi. It was our first time releasing a full fledged record, on a major label. It was our first time releasing videos alongside our work, and our first time really diving into the whirlwind that the music industry can be. 

We always tend to create far ahead of our next release, so as we began to show komorebi and ourselves to the world, we were processing our experiences and beginning to craft what we believed to be our next release. The earliest of songs were written in hotels ranging from Berlin to the Florida panhandle. We dreamed of a sleek, groove driven record, where subtle polyrhythms gave the listener a distinct head bop. We strove to expand our manipulations of guitars beyond the licks, lines and textures we’d established. For all of these inspired intentions, this record never saw the light of day, as our vision didn’t seem to resonate with our team at large.

‘night dive’ is such a meaningful song to bring to sound for our first drop here. it’s about the frustrations of the conventional music industry, where money and metrics seem to dictate movement more than an artist’s vision does. it’s a song that details how being fresh and new in a pre-existing system can be a toxic affair and a fast ride, leaving a person confused when they get out of the proverbial car. 
it’s a song that wasn’t able to surface back where we were, but has found a home here in web3 where art and community are valued. and for that we are very grateful

records.title: jealous
records.note:
Pollen is a project that originally started as a series of Zoom sessions and blossomed into 20 songs over the course of a few short months.

Collaboration can be a very hit or miss experience. Sometimes the vibe in a room can be off, sometimes the styles of genres simply don’t align. But when Lucas (Bloody White) and I (Daniel Allan) met, we immediately found a balance in working together. We quickly realized that we were both good at the things the other was bad at, so we began setting up sessions twice a week to work on as much music as we could. The music we were writing felt frictionless, honest, and timeless. It felt like we were exploring the dark side of my production and the light side of Lucas’.

After making an absurd amount of music, we came to the realization that we should start a band together. We started mood boarding, making even more music, and writing mission statements. We came up with our cross pollination strategy - the belief that the more genres we could intersect the less we had to bind ourselves to any one sound in pursuit of creative happiness. 

As $OVERSTIM started to change my life, Lucas began finding his early footing in Web3. Our attention became spread thin, and the timing of Pollen became more and more out of reach. But if there’s one thing we’ve both learned about Web3 it’s that overthinking can be a true Achilles heel, and good music deserves to be out in the world instead of locked on a hard drive.

Jealous is a song about paranoia in an unstable relationship.  Everybody knows what jealousy feels like in whatever form it may present itself.  It's a harsh, primal feeling.  The contrast between the lyrics and instrumental, for us, paints a picture of what it feels like to suppress and play off those doubtful thoughts.

To More.

records.title: wherever you go
records.note:
For those of you who don’t know me, my name is Jayden and I write music under TWERL. I’m originally from Perth, Western Australia but just relocated to Bali.

‘wherever you go’ is a track that’s extremely close to my heart as it’s an emotional collaboration with my partner Pauline that is about being in a long distance relationship and having to leave each other. I still remember the moment we were in a studio session in seperate rooms and she came in to play me the demo, I instantly teared up.

This is also a special moment as it’s my genesis Sound NFT and a further dive into web3 which is something that I’m extremely passionate about. records.title: The Only
records.note:
Hey everyone! I'm delighted to have my second drop on Sound, premiering a very special song.

I originally made The Only back in May 2022, right before my trip to LA. I was (and still am) heavily inspired by breakbeats and I wanted to combine those vibes with electric guitars, reese basses and acid synths. Being able to blend modern sounds with iconic rhythms has been my major goal for the whole year; this song aims to prove that.

The artwork is made by DVRS, my go to for any 3D visual I need and long time friend. I've been releasing many projects in collaboration with DVRS as I strongly believe in the importance of the audio / visual relationship. It's safe to say my music would impact way less without his art.

records.title: JOJO
records.note: hey i’m alec. from denver, in los angeles. this song is called jojo. it’s a first class seat on my train of thought through the rollercoaster of heartbreak. i’ve always wanted to do a song structured like this; a full beat switch. it’s an a side & b side of jojo. the perk of finally being an independent artist is that there is no chatter in my ears telling me “4 minutes is too long!” “jojo isn’t relatable enough for a song title!” “don’t use demo vocals” “why would you have a pig on a leash as the artwork, it doesn’t make sense!” i can keep going because this is fun but you get the point. i think this song encapsulates the experience of dealing with heartbreak while simultaneously having a career where you make those feelings very public. there is no other job where your next partner will know exactly how you felt about the last one. that’s jojo.

records.title: sunrise (ft. Lophiile)
records.note:
Sunrise is the third to last song on my upcoming debut album Dreaming of Flying. It feels like clarity after the dust settles, insight after heartbreak. I made it with Ty on the first day we met.

Every session I’ve ever had with another producer starts with a getting-to-know-you beat. We either sync up our DAWs or take turns on one computer and try to feel out what collaboration with eachother is like. Often these are sloppy and it takes until the second or third beat of the day for us to know how to best trust and compliment eachother. I still can’t believe this is the first thing we ever made together. It felt so easy and also fresh and new. I think that’s why I called it Sunrise.

This is the biggest step I’ve taken so far in building Dreaming of Flying. I make music everyday, therapeutically. So much of it never leaves my hard drive. Collectors of this project will have access to a monthly tape of my latest creations. Curated just for them. It means so much to me that you’re here. Thank you for listening.

records.title: Skyline
records.note:
Over the past 8 years huge range of different styles of music, and at times I’ve struggled with what to do with the ideas that didn’t quite fit the directions my artist project has taken. Music NFT’s have given me the space to share music that otherwise might never see the light of day with fans, and showcase other styles of music I love to make.

This track earned the title Skyline because when I listen to it I imagine floating around a snowy mountain or New York City at night, watching the world go by. Whenever writing music one my main focuses is to have contrasting moments - dreamy verses with soft, warping pads and then stripped, gritty choruses. I think this tune captures that perfectly.

records.title: Peanut Butter Cherry
records.note:
I really miss when Ludacris was in every DJs rotation. 'Peanut Butter Cherry' is me explaining how I am really missing everything that is nostalgic (for me, the late 2000s/early 2010s) while making sure the song (& myself) still feels good. 
PBC opens with my brain saying, "I been at this function, I been smoking something, idk who this is, guess we some hooligans, it's hard to get thru this shit, can you play some more Ludacris, cus it's hard to get through this shit" in a low pitched voice. Not sure if it is the devil or angel on my shoulder, but it is definitely telling me to leave this party and spend my time doing what I actually enjoy.
Shout out Luda

& again, thank you soooooooo much for making being an independent artist possible. this is very real

records.title: forever
records.note:
forever is the oldest and last song on my debut album, Dreaming of Flying.

I made it in 2018 before I even had the name Clear eyes for my solo project. It was initially more than double the BPM...I worked on it for a while and it didn't feel right. Then I slowed it all the way down until something clicked and this beautiful tapestry unfolded.

It sounded like nothing else I'd ever made, and I loved the way it made me feel. Centered, thoughtful, clear-headed. Slowing down the music made the world slow down for me. And I realized I'd stumbled into the most important feeling I wanted my solo project to evoke.

When you collect this sound, you join the world of Clear eyes and Dreaming of Flying. A world of music that makes you feel a particular way. A world I made for you.

yo! i’m peter! i’m an artist from the bay area, now livin in la! i make pop music and try to spread mental health awareness through everything i do! i’ve been playing guitar since i was 7 and grew up on literally everything from worship music, to classic rock, blues, pop, etc. i’m heavily inspired by people like john mayer, the 1975, lewis capaldi, and honestly all of my friends. during my senior year of high school i made my first song and put it out for my friends and family to hear. it ended up getting on some pretty cool playlists and hit 100,000 plays on Spotify alone within the first couple months of its release, and it honestly changed my life—the response i got from the song was just insane… i received hundreds of dm’s from people saying how much the song had affected their life. it wasn’t until that song came out, that i had realized how much potential there was to make an impact on youth culture through my music. a few months later though, i had ended up losing my brother in law to suicide in 2018. the last thing he posted on his facebook page was a link to stream my first song. it was an insanely rough time for me, my family, and everyone around me. it broke us. as i kept making music over the years though, i’ve received thousands and thousands of dm’s, mostly from random people saying that my music had really helped them. at this point, i’m still thinking to myself that maybe if i wrote some of these songs earlier--that maybe my brother in law would still be here?  those dm’s i received, conversations i had, etc. have really put a lot on my heart and a ton of purpose in my soul to continue doing what i'm doing. i truly hope that you can connect with my music and that it can give you an escape to help you build new perspectives. 

this song i am dropping, “wishing”, is one of the more recent songs i’ve made. i wrote it about the idea of being in a relationship where BOTH of you are toxic. you're always breaking up, getting back together, acting like you don't care when you really do, etc. and for some reason you can't seem to make the final decision to just walk away and end things. i wrote it in hopes of inspiring you to stop letting yourself stay in pointless situations where you're constantly hurt, over & over. i hope you stop "wasting your life" away with unnecessary BS… whether that be your relationships, your job, etc. 
also i’m wishin that you’ll dig this song <3

records.title: King Of The Slum
records.note:
I am a multi-disciplinary artist from Chicago; my primary medium is hip-hop music. I was born and raised on the South Side with family roots in Ghana, West Africa. Growing up I was a skateboarder first, a graffiti artist second and a rapper third, music quickly becoming the fabric that tied all poles of my life together and gave me contextual meaning. The ethos of my creativity is truth telling; to share my unique perspective through the various mediums I employ.

The song King Of The Slum was made during my recent stay in Ghana in January. I titled it as such in reference to the slum in which my family resides and my father was born, known as Asokore Zongo in Koforidua. Zongo settlements are largely poverty stricken areas in West African towns comparable in ways to the Black American ghetto, albeit much less resourced. Much of the lyrical content of this song speaks to the juxtaposition of these different sides of my existence. My uncle, who lives in the zongo, is a legendary Ghanian musician named Chief Kofi Sammy of the Okukuseku International Band, and a pioneer of a style of music called High Life. For this record, which I also produced, I took influence from the music of my ancestry while I was physically in my homeland to manipulate some traditional melodic elements within the framework of my own personal style.

The photograph out of which I made the cover is of myself in the Zongo with my nieces and nephews. Despite the extreme poverty experienced where my family lives, there is immense power in culture and spirituality that I have sought to express through my practice in both photography and music.

records.title: Phone Tag
records.note:
My name’s Camden - I’m an alt soul artist originally from a tiny town called Greenville, Illinois.  I never thought music was a practical career, and none of my friends were pursuing it, but eventually the idea of doing anything else felt like being trapped in a cage.  Once I swallowed my fear of failure, I moved to the closest music industry city I could, Nashville. 

Growing up, I always gravitated toward jazz and soul music, but when I went to record, the sound never felt right.  I hadn’t discovered “my” way of doing it yet.  So I focused on writing for other people, and got to explore a lot of different sounds that way.  Later, I went on a songwriting trip to London, and felt like my artist project came to life there.  

Phone Tag is a result of my time in the UK.  R&B/soul melodies placed over futuristic production sets the tone for nostalgic lyrics about love that never happened.

records.title: Too Late (To Call)
records.note:
The story of this song starts over a year ago now, on the day that the sky turned dark red in the Bay Area. 

Thanks to smoke from nearby wildfires, our beautiful home had been converted into a hellscape overnight. It was definitely surreal, but oddly bittersweet as well, as it kind of forced us to reminisce about the world we saw ending all around us. 

Whenever we’re forced to acknowledge that some phase of our life is ending (whether it be school, a job, or the f*cking world), it’s hard to not think about all the things we wish we’d done differently. “Too Late” is what happens when you let yourself get swept up in that nostalgia––it’s that one last futile transmission into the vacuum.

For this song, we drew a lot of inspiration from anthemic pop songs, pulling melodies and rhythms that feel good and contrast well with the melancholic lyrics. 

“Too Late” has already brought us so much love and joy; we hope it can do the same for you <3

records.title: Stems & Twigs Mix
records.note:
The “Amen break” is one of music’s most beloved and essential samples, ranking up there with “Funky Drummer” and “Think (About It)” as the most used breaks in hip-hop and electronic music. However, the primary songwriters behind the track – the Winstons’ Richard L. Spencer, who wrote the arrangement for the song and owned the copyright on the track, and drummer Gregory Coleman, who died homeless in 2006 – never received royalties from their indispensable beat.

I always wanted to find a way to credit the creators behind the samples I was using in my own productions. It’s easy to do so on a vinyl sleeve (and I did), but the music streaming industry doesn’t care, and makes it almost impossible to share informations about a record and how it was produced, apart from the main artist’s name. Most of us know that there’s more to a record than just a singer, a rapper, or a techno producer. Music is inherently collaborative. Music is the fabric of communities. Music is made of shared moments, connections, and interactions. 

The Stems & Twigs Mix is an experiment in collaborative creative processes, using smart contracts to ensure that all creators are credited and get a fair share of the sale, based on how much they’ve contributed

Following the Ensemble Mix (the first ever techno DJ set minted as an NFT back in March 2022 on sound.xyz), I decided to push forward by putting together a mix based, not on finished songs, but on stems (individual instrumental tracks). 

After announcing the idea on Twitter, I received around 550 different stems, uploaded on a shared folder : drum loops, basslines, vocals, guitars, synthesizers, sfx, or even modular and generative experiments. Each stem file’s name needed to include a twitter handle and an ETH wallet address 

I spent the next week assembling these components into a 25 minutes piece of music where almost every sound has been sourced from this collective sample pool. From the 550 stems originally received, 46 have been used in the mix (I only included 4 of my own stems). The final mix will be sold on sound.xyz as an NFT with multiple editions. Each producer will receive a percentage of the NFT sale, based on how many of his stems have been used (1 stem = 1%), with 50% of the sale going to the stem producers, and 50% to myself for building the mix and designing the concept. 

What’s interesting is that, even if 92% of the building blocks I used were produced by other musicians, the mix sounds a lot like a typical Maelst

records.title: about you (with Nightly)
records.note:
'about you' is a very special song to us that marks a transition in our creative process, one that has been a long time in the making. earlier in our career, we had commercial success in the dance pop world, but as time went on we felt that our inspiration to make those kinds of records was fading. at the same time, we wanted to evolve our sound. although we didn’t know exactly where we wanted to go, we did feel the urge to go back to our musical roots in some way — growing up listening to rock bands and playing instruments from a very young age.

we decided to try dm’ing a few bands that we were big fans of, including Nightly, to see if it would spark anything. Nightly actually answered and sent over a batch of toplines, which included 'about you', and something clicked in our heads. we started working on the production immediately, and the song was finished in a few months, all done over the internet.

in the time that has passed since the song was finished in 2019, we have followed the rise of NFTs, and even more interestingly for us, music NFTs. as producer-heads who love gaming and learning about new tech, we've been watching closely as the space has grown so quickly. the concept first caught our eye when BossLogic, a visual artist who we were working on another project with, started doing nft drops in early 2021. we then learned about music nft’s and soon became collectors.

as awareness of nft's grew, we continued to experiment with the "new" NOTD sound that we first discovered with 'about you' and this year we are lining up to share a new chapter of music with our fans. we’d be lying if we didn’t say that for a while, we questioned our place in the music nft world. a major label changed our lives when we were 16 and 18 years old and we'll always be grateful for that opportunity, but we've also seen the ins and outs of a system that is not working for the majority of artists. to their credit though, our label gave us their blessing on this drop.

at the end of the day, we want to continue creating art that inspires us and build a community of supporters who can also now be collectors. it feels very symbolic that ‘about you’ is both the song that kickstarted our inspiration for this new chapter of music and also the song for our first nft drop.

records.title: FLASHLIGHT
records.note:
Flashlight is a song about life’s obstacles and how we can maneuver through those struggles whilst remaining confident in ourselves. Aaron & I were just beginning our musical journey together and were scrolling through some sketches he made one day. I remember my jaw dropping to the floor when he played this one. I didn’t have any lyrics or melody right away but I knew it was something special. I lived with it for some time, life happened and stories were born. During one of our hourglass sessions we brought this one up and melodies started to come in the form of scats. When the time was right I finally had a chorus, “Ain’t there but I’m on my way, I’m almost there, I’ll be okay” a true and simple mantra that we can all relate to.
	Some months later, after some hard losses and realizations, I had what I needed to finish the rest of the lyrics. With the intro & verse I wanted to shine light on the failures instead of trying to hide/ignore them, hence the “flashlight” reference. That truthfulness with Self was so helpful I couldn’t help but feel grateful, blessed even, about all the things that didn’t work out. All those doors that shut somehow lead us to greater things. When we take note of that, it’s a little easier to tell ourselves, and actually believe, that we’ll be okay.
	Once the rest of the vocals were in, Aaron went back into the music to experiment with arrangement, adding dynamics, and sculpting the sounds until it amplified the message loud enough so the whole world could hear it. We joke about the music feeling like a giant gold-plated tank that shoots flowers instead of bullets. That’s the energy we tapped into for this track and the rest of the songs on our upcoming EP “3RDWIND”.

records.title: Password
records.note:
Sometimes the only way out is through. Civilizations in ruin tell stories of prideful men burning bridges & passing judgment. I inhaled the ashes of the aftermath as visions of the past became clear. A guardian angel descended upon my ancestors, exiling them from the place they called home. A golden blade carved out the foundation of the castle walls and suspended it above the clouds for no man, woman, or child to ever return.

Centuries have passed since then, yet the paradigms remain. At my birth I was given a pendant in the shape of a key by an elderly traveler. My grandmother told me it resembled a legendary sword. I carried it with me for decades never knowing its true power. But the day you and I met, I experienced an awakening; a burning sensation beneath my feet. Warring kingdoms became our thoughts. The battlefield, our conversations. The pen is mightier than the sword but the power of life and death is in the tongue. In truth you were sent to destroy me, but as time passed we found happiness in one another. You returned to your homeland only to be deemed a failure and executed. But love is not blind. It sees you in the dark and chooses to be your light. 

An emotional outburst to the news of your departure created a rift in the earth beneath our feet. From the dust appeared the key of legend. What I believed to be visions, were in fact memories of reincarnation. The guardian angel in human form, cast down from the Eternal Garden to endure pain, suffering, and heartbreak. 

Oh, how much I’ve learned. In my agony, I cursed my enemies. I sought out revenge. The trials by which I judged humanity, even I could not conquer. I learned that the heart is fragile, but love is the password to every soul.

So in this life, I use this key, like Cupid’s arrow — to restore the Earth. 

--

records.title: Fever Dream
records.note:
My name is Kate Ellwanger, and I make music as Dot. I'm originally from Olympia, WA, and now spend my time between Los Angeles and Ketchum, Idaho. 

"Fever Dream" is the first single from my new EP, and each song on the project represents a different type of battle I've fought with grief and depression over the past year. While the instrumental of this song has a brighter and easygoing feel, the lyrics hint at some darkness underneath the glossy exterior. 

The song paints a surrealistic picture of a person's desire to wake up from the dream states so many of us live in, but going about it in all the wrong ways -- through self-destructive behavior and romanticized substance abuse. It follows the main character on a road trip from LA to Las Vegas, with the lyrics becoming more and more nonsensical and drifting further from reality as the music progresses. 

I wrote this song as a reminder to myself that seeking altered states through those shortcuts will never lead you to true fulfillment or wakefulness -- they just keep you in a feedback loop of dishonest self-reflection, and searching for more highs that ultimately take you nowhere. 

I think this message is especially important during a time when so many of us are trying to find meaning in our lives, but what we see spread across the news and on our timelines devalues human life on so many levels. It's easier to take on a carefree "yolo" mentality in this environment than to truly show love to ourselves and the people around us, because the cognitive dissonance becomes so overwhelming amidst current events.

My name is Mark Johns, I’m an artist living in LA and have been making music since 2015.

I wrote this on the piano in my room a couple years ago and immediately ran downstairs to bang on my neighbor Brenton’s door. He was in a session with our friend AO beats and I basically hijacked it, begging them to help me turn the piano into guitar. We recorded the whole thing in less than 20 minutes. I cried a bunch and that was it.

Anytime I wanted to put it out I was talked out of it by somebody telling me that there wasn’t enough in it to latch on to. What even is the hook here, there’s no drums, the guitar sounds like ass etc etc etc. I had no interest in changing it so I just never released it.

It sucked cause songs like ‘I’m sorry’ are the songs that I feel like a part of me is embedded in. They are the ones that take 20 minutes to write because you don’t need to think when you’re telling the truth.

Feels special for this to be my genesis NFT, and I truly appreciate every single one of you who takes the time to listen.

My path in music has been one of gradual progressions - from classical piano lessons at 3 years old, to singing and playing in school talent shows, to writing, recording, cutting my teeth with 4 hour bar gigs and local venue shows, to touring, to producing, and learning a lot along the way. When the pandemic started, my journey in production hit a stride and I dove deeper than ever. In the last 6 months, the latest challenge to myself was to write and produce songs from conception to completion solely on my own. To be able to if I wanted. I love collaboration and need it as a creative, but self-sufficiency and personal growth has been crucial to my sustainability as an independent artist.

Enter “Good Day To You”. It started with a beat I made on one my favorite keyboards, the OP-1 by Teenage Engineering. I’m inspired by sounds and mood, and that beat set the tone for the rest of the track. This is also my first released song playing live bass.

You know when ‘words don’t do it justice’? That applies to people too. And sometimes no matter what you say, even if warranted, your value and worth may not be seen by someone in the way it should. In that case, silence is sometimes the most respectful action towards yourself and the most appropriate for someone who doesn’t deserve any more of your time.

i started this song in the fall of 2021 after a fight with a family member. i felt so misunderstood and frustrated by how childish and inconsequential the fight was - on my way home i wrote the first lyric “you said some things you never meant that you thought you did.” as time passed, the fight that started with my family member shifted to one between me and myself. i was so disappointed at how much energy i let the entire situation take from me - the song became as much about a fight with myself as it is about a fight with someone else.  

in that moment i was certain that my relationships with my family member & myself would forever be deeply altered. but nothing actually changed - my wounds were just paper cuts. i wrote the lyric “you don’t hurt like you think you do, like a bug but i just scratch right through” - and the rest of the song fell into place. i realized i wasn’t writing about being angry or disappointed - i was writing about the power and amusement of realizing your own strength.

i produced the bones of the song as i wrote it. as the emotion of the song changed, i tried to make the song’s darker, grittier elements to work in a light, playful way - the muted guitars and distorted bass line still drive the song, but the chord changes feel less serious. i sent the entire project over to my friend struan finlay in new zealand to fill out the rest of the production.

records.title: Demons
records.note:
hello, i’m alara. i’m a singer-songwriter and visual artist from new jersey. 

music has always been a part of my life. i began writing songs when i was 11 and taught myself guitar all throughout high school. i've always felt like i didn't belong and creating music was the best way for me to express that emotion. to express all emotions. it was a world i created where i could escape. growing up as a child of immigrant parents, i never saw being a musician as a viable career choice until one and a half years into medical school when i decided that i had to try. i spent almost every night for a year playing open mics in new york city, building a community of artists who made me feel like i wasn't alone for the first time. that year made me realize making music wasn't a choice, it's something i had to do.

fast forward to november of last year. i was just learning about NFTs for the first time and spending every free moment immersing myself in the world of web3. the idea that artists could finally break the confines of the traditional music industry drew me in almost immediately. i'd like my experiences here to convince the 15-year old indian girl struggling to play barre chords in her east coast bedroom that she can be a musician if she wants to be. 

taking inspiration from artists like thom yorke and damien rice, my sound has evolved as i learn more about who i am. i wrote “demons” as a way to tell myself that it's alright to be vulnerable. this song is as much for me as it is for someone very close to me. it’s about finding solace in the idea that everyone is going through something. your demons may not look like mine, but we shouldn’t be afraid to admit that they exist. we shouldn't be afraid to open up. 

i hope it helps you in some way.

records.title: Just Like Me
records.note:
hi my name is ben :) i am an artist & producer based in philadelphia. i have been making music in the same corner of my parents’ basement for as long as i can remember. i started releasing music in late 2019 - i had been writing & producing for other artists for years but nothing ever felt good enough or special enough or me enough to release myself. i was a senior in college and terrified of failure but more terrified of entering the real world without a career. i will always remember how liberating and validating those first few releases were - i don’t naturally share a lot but i fell in love with the challenge of being vulnerable in public

and then COVID hit - all of the stability and validation that i had cherished began to fade. while my friends were starting new lives in new cities with new jobs, i was moving back in with my parents. a lot of the anxiety and self doubt that i had kept at bay for so long crept up - i spent a lot of time in 2021 confronting the baggage that comes with pursuing a creative life. and i spent a lot of time writing about how music & my career ambitions have played into past relationships 

she was also pursuing a creative career - that was our glue but also our downfall. it is comforting to be with someone who shares your dreams and insecurities. but it can also be intense. and confusing. it wasn’t until i sat down to write with my friend jono (julius black) that the line “could i fix your heart if i fix mine?” fell out and things began to make sense - trying to love someone who is just like you is hard

records.title: SUNLIGHT
records.note:

Sunlight pulls inspiration from a lot of the music that I was listening to and was inspired by when I first began creating wavs. There's something beautiful about that youthful time and energy for me. It feels good to go back and start pulling from that place again.

Music is some of my favorite first memories as a child. My parents were free spirits who took me to countless live gigs and organically, it was the medium I gravitated most to in my life. When I was three years old, I begged my grandma for a mini drum set, since my parents couldn't afford it. Somehow, we found a child-size drum kit for me to start making noise. This was the start of my journey of learning multiple instruments and finding my voice in this language of music.

I grew up playing in bands and recording music from a very young age and always felt the hunger to create. When I started making music on my computer, I fell down the Ableton rabbit hole and it shifted what I thought was possible with music, beyond the things I had been doing in my bands. Not just sonically, but also from a self-reliance point of view. I wanted to see what it would be like to take from that original youthful sonic quality and energy. 

This song takes inspiration from my band days and live instrumentation background, and fuses it with my electronic music experience (using a computer as an instrument). I take a seasonality approach to life and have been in a season of abundant music creation, which reminds me of the child-like wonder I had when I first started making music. This song attempts to capture a piece of that into an audio wav.

I feel in a similar place creatively to when I was younger and more naive, but without the naivety that stops you from actualizing your creations. My hope is for that child-like wonder to spread into the WRLD.

Like most musicians, my catharsis was the wavs that emerged into this song.

LYFE is a song about the human experience, our relationship with time and what we choose to do with it. Do we waste it? What is wasting it? What is the best way to pass the time? What does dwelling on the past do for us? Should we be dwelling on the past? Is the past just a memory in the present moment? What should we be orienting ourselves towards, in order to create meaning in our lives and the lives of others?

records.title: Sorry CVS
records.note:
Helloooo hellooo! For those who don’t know me, I’m Lyrah :) I’m a writer/producer/singer based in LA.

I originally grew up in Pennsylvania, in a sleepy, small town that kinda forced you to find your own source of entertainment (hello music). I played piano since I was 3 and was singing at everything from church to skate park shows. Fast forward to college, when I started writing toplines for EDM, toured with a band as their keyboardist, and started to teach myself how to produce. And now today I love making my own music that feels like someone’s personal soundtrack in a sad but dancey world.


It’s hard to write about this song, because the song was intentionally written to never state the very thing it’s about — cancer.

But to truly know the song, you need to know the backstory.

A few months ago, my brother started experiencing some health issues. His doctors weren’t concerned and even denied requests for booking any additional testing. My mom got on the phone with his doctor and begged, yet nothing changed. My brother and parents independently secured an appointment.

We went from a doctor refusing to schedule any testing to a stage 4 cancer diagnosis.

From shows like “Breaking Bad” you imagine that someone sits you down and creates a space for you while you process difficult news. But instead, you get results uploaded to your chart for you to interpret on your own. A few days later a doctor will call to say “I’m so sorry” and they’ll bill that 5 minute phone call to your insurance. And then you’ll pay your $20 co-pay for a call you’ll never forget.

The healthcare system often feels so criminal. In response to this, my mom joked that we should just start stealing things. When we went to CVS later that day, I may or may not have stolen a pack of peanut m&ms to make her happy.

That night I went to my brother’s apartment. And while he played guitar, I told him about the peanut m&m adrenaline rush of the day. I joked to his girl friend (now wife!) that we should just write about stealing from CVS but then that’s exactly what we did. The chorus was the first thing we wrote and verse 2 flowed out fast behind it:

records.title: Number
records.note:
My name is SLOE JACK. I’m a nineteen-year-old punk/pop artist from Melbourne, Australia.

My debut track, “Number”, outlines heartbreak, betrayal and how difficult it can be to trust someone after being stabbed in the back. Meeting people after a bad relationship is basically just red flag hunting, a search for reasons to flee the scene to defend yourself from previous traumas. When I wrote this song I wanted the lyrics to be blatant and honest. We’re talking about straight-up relationship anxiety here, so why not lay it out bare.

All I used to listen to as a kid was dubstep. As a result of listening to straight square waves for my entire childhood, I have an instinctual and inhuman urge to distort every sound I throw at my track, no matter the genre. People ask me, “how do I achieve the SLOE JACK sound?” All you gotta do is disregard all production standards and get weird.

Big thanks to the Sound team for giving me this opportunity and to Dreams Never Die for releasing my debut track! I feel so fortunate to be involved in the first season of Sound and I will never forget this moment.

records.title: LIGHTS OFF
records.note:
(Madi) One evening this past fall of 2021, I was at odds; I was feeling particularly uninspired and exhausted by the music industry. I distinctly remember sitting out on my patio at an absurdly late hour; scrolling through my likes hoping that I could revive an old gem, and I rediscovered Rob’s music. We had made a song named “Alibi” together with our friend Pham a few years ago, but hadn’t talked since then. I spent most of the night listening, and so naturally, I reached out to him to see what he was up to...

We reconnected and formed an organic bond creating art and talking about our music industry trauma. We made over thirty songs within just a couple of weeks while simultaneously terrorizing each other in Minecraft and brainstorming the early ideas that became this project. Our friend Dan (aka elozi) had a demo named “GLOWSTONE” that we sampled to make “LIGHTS OFF''. The name felt right for our project and our partnership created a strong foundation that enabled us to start building our own world.

“LIGHTS OFF” is a song about the drastic highs-to-lows phenomena of life. It illustrates not only the pain but the embrace of change, particularly from an artist’s point of view, which we believe a lot of artists can relate with.

records.title: fumes
records.note:
As an artist who jumps around from genre to genre, I found that I hadn’t dropped a lot of acoustic records. I write so many songs just to guitar and produce them out once I’ve done my thing, but I never release them stripped. And with a rock project on the horizon I figured now would be an amazing time to let go a record like Fumes.

I wrote this record in my bedroom and wanted to make it feel classic and timeless, but also spicy. It’s about trying to keep up with someone you’re captivated by even if their life moves a little faster than yours. It’s crazy what we do for love… or lust. I mean who hasn’t gotten high just to impress someone they’re feeling, knowing damn well it’s going to make the rest of the night an anxious whirlwind of overthinking. Lord knows I have and I’ll do it again.

I came up with the hook while hanging at my place with my homie Miles Wesley. We bounced off each other until we dialled in a hook that felt perfect even without any production behind it. Later on when I was alone I freestyled on the mic for verse ideas until the verse was done. When I’m trying to give a song the secret sauce and have it feel fresh I generally don’t write anything down and come up with everything while recording. This song is cool to me because I mixed classic songwriting (just me and Miles singing in the room while he strummed the guitar) and my hiphop driven, off the cuff style of freestyle writing.

After the song was written I had my producer homies finish the music, get the guitar sounding perfect and add some subtle textures around the vocals. Shoutouts Tarro, Zailor and Blake Straus. Then I had the vocal goat Chris “TEK” O’Ryan mix it and get me sounding crispy but also keep it very honest and true. And finally, I got it mastered by the best in the game, Becker.
