records.title: CULTURE
records.note:
So after working with a publishing label that was treating me like I was a slave, I got stuck in form and this idea that songwriting has to be one way, I took some time to heal because I really couldn’t write for months. To help, I decided to ride my bike to clear my head, and one day I envisioned myself rapping a verse on the L.A. River. And that’s how “Joyride” came to life. 

“Joyride” is an evolving practice of free verses that are straight to it. No form, just me and me philosophies in bars. It’s a meditation, it’s short bits of me, it’s whatever you want to make it. An opportunity to just allow myself to ride the beat. To create these verses, I would start with a beat I love, rap on it and then send the accapella to Kaui to create something new out of it.

“Culture”, this first offering/verse off of “Joyride” came to me after rapping on Kaytranada’s production. I wrote the verse in a nite and immediately knew I didn’t want to add much else to it. I am very lyrical and I am realizing, sometimes one verse is enough. Sometimes keeping it simple is all you need. Sometimes just riding your own path is what I have to do. 

So this year as I’m riding my path, I guess I’m using this “Joyride” as an exercise in getting back to me, getting out of my way, sticking to my journey, continuing to create with bro Kaui who has been working with me for years, I’m really excited for how this ride will take me to more paths.  Next up “Showtime”

records.title: over u
records.note:
As someone who writes songs as therapy, I find myself writing almost every single day. However I might not be going through something new to talk about each day so the challenge is finding different angles from which to attack the same emotions. It helps my brain understand what my heart is feeling when I force myself to articulate it from many perspectives. Some are more on the nose and some a bit more ambiguous.

At the time when I wrote “over u” I was stuck in a major label record deal that wasn’t lining up with the expectations I had pre signing. That scary moment when your dreams come true but leave you feeling even more lost than before. This song is me writing and singing to “music” and my career as if it were a person I was in a relationship with. Thoughts of throwing in the towel mixed with memories of all the nights I struggled and battled mental illness with no one to talk to but the microphone. At the end of it all I am back independent and happy as I’ve ever been with a new found insight on why I make music and what my journey is all about.

Produced by my brother Tarro
Mixed & Mastered by Elijah Woods

records.title: find my line
records.note:
some of the best things in life evolve naturally and organically. relationships blossom. love blossoms. intimacy blossoms when you allow it to naturally blossom. "find my line" is to me a sonic representation of that exact feeling. that amazing moment where you find the perfect way to show this other person that you want them and you're theirs if they want you too. Whether it's something you say, a gesture with your body language, or a mix of the two It's very subtle, but powerful. There's this spark in that moment and it's one that lights a fire in the special moment you share. There's a trust and vulnerability you share in that moment. Whether you're single or in a relationship the moment exists. If you're like me, engaged and in a relationship for 5+ years, that fire always remains because the bond I share with my partner is so deep and true. Those special moments are even more powerful because we get to exclusively share them for the rest of our lives together. 

writing "find my line" was just as organic. It flowed so naturally, from the writing, to the production, to the recording to the mixing/mastering. There was a bit of pressure leading up the moment everything flowed, but once it finally struck I believe I found my own version of a diamond. I hope you think so too. thanks for listening.

records.title: AMERICAN GURL
records.note:
Hi!

I'm Kish Robinson — a multidisciplinary artist, director, and performer working in music, film, and the written word. My most extensive project is KILO KISH, a solo music project spanning ten years of exploring internal and external identities and socio-cultural expectations.      

AMERICAN GURL is the title track of my next album coming out this March. This album explores the power of choice, finding personal freedoms, and escaping imposed old notions and identities. I made this with my collaborator Ray Brady, on multiple writing trips to Joshua Tree, CA, between 2019-2020.       

This song speaks to the rat race and static systems that keep us in a rut. I'm always trying to overcome my own history, explore black history's weight, and overcome the need to be a success story, an achiever, and a good example. I've been wondering how to redefine freedom and success. I've been boxed in throughout my career by race, womanhood, age, and experience level, which has made my practice sometimes feel like running headfirst at a brick wall. But I always imagine a place where artists can feel singular and free. I made this work to detoxify myself from what others expected of me. 

I created the cover collage from my collection of vintage postcards, which I repurposed along with my image. These postcards represent memories and moments of others, some even written out to loved ones. Now, they're thrust into the present and meshed with my experience decades later. The image is one of many iterations in this style and a part of my American Gurl Series — A collection of digital artworks and films. 

Americanism is a hazy myth, a web of so many different backgrounds, archetypes, and iconography that I can try on for size through my music and art. Working digitally, film images from the past connects and tethers our American experience summing up my understanding of it as a whole. Exploring these concepts as NFTs and in the web3 space brings them even further into the future. 

I’m excited to share! I hope you enjoy the song and images!

records.title: Taurus
records.note:
Making music over the past couple years has presented a bit of a challenge.
Finding something worthwhile to put out into the world, against all the noise, while just trying to make sense of my own reactions to it felt at times impossible.

Taurus, the lead single on my new EP Fantasy, was born out of a desire for literal escapism, as well as a beacon of light of my own. From the walls of my apartment to a sprawling forest somewhere.

Many lockdowns ago, in my old apartment in Toronto, clawing my way in and out of depression and a kind of survival mode, I tried to force myself into a routine, to make something, anything, to fill the emptiness of daily life.

I reached out to Joel Ford, who had mixed my last album Dawn Chorus and became a good friend since, for advice on how to go about it. Through him I started talking to Leanne Macomber, and we started trading some simple musical sketches. I think the relative loneliness of lockdown in Canada spurred a desire for collaboration as well as the literal presence of a human voice on the record. I’d send her simple chord progressions, a few key words and then start cutting up what she sent back.

One of the main goals of this record was to undo fully formed narrative arcs from my tracks, to make stuff that felt like it was ‘floating’ a bit more. Like an ambient character-and-mood-driven scene as opposed to expeditionary dialogue and action. 
The result is a track that ebbs and flows, and hopefully can help someone else through this too.

records.title: Rainy Daze
records.note:
2022 marks the ten-year anniversary of Poolside's iconic debut album Pacific Standard Time. To celebrate, Poolside will be commemorating the album by releasing 'Rainy Daze', a lost b-side from the album. The track features all of the sonic hallmarks of Poolside: a Poolside mid-tempo groove beneath hand claps, floating synths, and laid back guitar and piano. 

Pacific Standard Time – released (10) years ago this July and coming back in print for the first time in (5) years – is an essential record of the 2010s. One of the first albums to bridge the gap between indie and electronic music, PST is the progenitor of "nu-disco", and more specifically the first document of Poolside's "Daytime Disco" sound. PST includes Poolside's signature tracks "Harvest Moon" and "Do You Believe", and since its release the record has amassed upwards of 300mm streams across all platforms. In 2012 Pitchfork called PST "dance music for the chillout tent", perfectly predicting the trends that would follow in PST's wake as dance music became more accessible in the streaming era.

Poolside is the recording project of producer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Jeffrey Paradise. Poolside has released four acclaimed albums – Pacific Standard Time (2012), Heat (2017), Low Season (2020) and High Season (2021) – remixed countless high-profile acts such as Billy Idol, Jack Johnson & Milky Chance, Purple Disco Machine, Rhye, L'Impératrice, DRAMA, Miami Horror and more, and toured the world over performing at major festivals across the globe including Coachella, Outside Lands, Primavera and Corona Capital as well as supporting marquee artists like LCD Soundsystem, Kacey Musgraves and Tycho.

records.title: Wavelength
records.note:
After a hiatus from my personal music, I found myself falling into the same old patterns of production. I had a standard process - writing chords, into drums, into an ABC arrangement that was all too safe after months of needing to start ideas quickly in my sessions.

Over my career, a few tracks and experiences have marked breakthroughs in my creative process. Wavelength is one of those tracks.

This track started with a few demo guitar riffs and chords by my good friend, glass tux. After hearing it and polishing up the chords, I knew I had to turn this into something outside of my comfort zone. 

Here is a track, with my humble take, on textures, ear candy, swing, and all of the finer details of production that I usually omit in favor staying in my melodic comfort zone. I've learned so much more from this track, and I hope you enjoy Wavelength as much as I did working on it.

- Jeffrey aka Poolside

my first drop on this site took place while i was in Malibu at a writing camp put on by Daniel Allan.  at the camp i was surrounded by a variety of artists, each with their own skill sets, backgrounds, and techniques.  it was exhausting, but just what i needed.  

for months leading up to the camp i was stuck in a very trying relationship.  this took up most of my mental bandwidth.  i couldn't seem to finish a single song.  it drove me fucking crazy.  a switch flipped for me at the camp.  i noticed quickly that each of these artists had their own very specific way of doing things.  it would be nearly impossible to find parallels between their workflows.  working alongside them reminded me that there are no right answers in art.  "how does it feel?" is the only question worth my concern.

immediately upon returning home, i started writing again.  i was met with that beautiful mania that only takes hold when i'm working on something meaningful to me.  i was finishing songs again, and fast.  this is the first of many.

A wise man once said you can never have both; you’re either too busy or too broke for the move. Regardless of the industry or type of labor, most people have to work some kind of job to sustain themselves even though it isn’t necessarily always what they want to be doing. Although it creates financial stability, it can also be physically, mentally, and (in some cases) emotionally draining. This may prevent you from pursuing things you actually want to do. In the perfect world, everyone would be a millionaire doing something they love. But in a not so perfect but very real world that we actually live in, the goal is to find a balance between two essential things that don’t always coexist well.

records.title: Be?
records.note:
“Be?” is the outro to our recently released debut album “Are We Here?” The song is about uncertainty both as an artist and as people in life as we know it. The question marks symbolize the uncertainty and the words themselves, “be” and, “are we here” represent the existential crises we have experienced throughout our journey both individually and together as a duo.

Growing up as first generation Nigerian & Pakistani children in Silver Spring, Maryland, it was obvious that our family and extended family wanted the best for us. However, it was not always obvious that the vision that they had for our lives was congruent with the vision that we saw for ourselves. It became common practice for us to live a double life, veiled between the person that we are in our families and the people we would like to be in the world. We wanted to be artists and they wanted us to be doctors, lawyers, engineers, and anything alike. Our pursuits in the arts we're not only unwelcomed but often discouraged. This led to us feeling small, unwanted, and outcasted by the very people that we call family. This life of duality eventually began causing a rift in our identities and started pulling away at the very fabric of our personality. We decided that, as difficult as it may be, it is always best to embrace your true self and to chase after your dreams.

Pursuing your dreams doesn’t always lead to happiness; we found that out fairly soon lol. We also found out that becoming and being an artist comes with its own set of challenges. A set of challenges that were not so far away in nature from the challenges of our cultural upbringing. To be an artist is to exist in duality; the ups and the downs, the private and the public, the individual and the collective, the confidence and the critique, the questions and the answers... This spectrum of everyday existence for artists contributes to the everyday plight of finding the balance between unflappable confidence and crippling self-doubt. Then we started to realize that duality isn’t necessarily good or bad… it just is. Through the means of our constant creations, we realized that how we navigate through these conflicting existences is what makes us, us.

records.title: wolf
records.note:
as a young(er) kid i always had a hard time expressing myself verbally.  trying to articulate my thoughts felt like an impossible task.  i never had an appropriate or effective medium for expression.  i knew that music spoke to me.  i distinctly remember at the age of 8 my sister putting on a song about a man on his deathbed.  i couldn’t fully grasp the weight of what the singer was saying, but i felt the emotion in his voice and especially in the instrumental.  that’s when it clicked for me.  music is a universal language.  

two years later i went to the movies with my family.  we watched Tron Legacy.  as a kid, i loved all the action and visual effects, but what really stuck with me was the soundtrack.  i hadn’t heard anything like it up to that point.  i was hooked.  from there, diving into daft punk, deadmau5, skrillex, porter robinson and many others, it was only a matter of time before i arrived at the realization that there were infinite possible ways to express oneself sonically by using just a laptop and some headphones.  the rest is history, as they say.  i’ve been using music as my primary form of expression for 10 years now.  every song i write is a personal challenge, emotionally and technically.  a welcomed one.  it’s been indescribably cathartic to get to a place where other people care about and can relate to what i have to say through my music.  i’m very thankful that anybody listens at all and i’m very excited for the journey ahead.  

wolf is about being lied to.  wether it be your partner, parents, a friend, politicians, 
or “society” as a whole, we’ve all been lied to.  i grew up pretty sheltered.  my parents tried their best to shield me from the harsh realities of life.  i had no idea how bad things could get, and surely i’m still ignorant of how fucked up things can become.  my parents divorce was ugly.  my parents aren’t bad people, but they both showed their true colors in many regards.  i quickly started to become aware of the flaws both of them kept from me through every step of my upbringing.  when those you trusted and held in such high regard morally turn out to be no better than you in their own ways, it calls a lot of things into question.  this is what it feels like.

records.title: IPHONE
records.note: We made iPhone as the first track for my crowdfund project “Your High Horse”. I went to Atlanta like the first week we launched it and we immediately pumped out this song in about an hour or two. This was one of those rare occasions where I knew exactly how I was going to approach the song off rip. The idea was thematically inspired by “Device Control” by Frank Ocean + “Everybody Nose” by NERD and it’s one of those records where I wanted to paint a picture in a tongue in cheek way about the way we all use our phones. The idea is that there’s two people in the bathroom at the club (supposed to be having a good time) complaining on social media about having to go out and then on the flip end, how we complain about how we’d rather be on our phones than in the moment and how we all have this obsession with portraying something that’s not accurate to the rest of the world.… how we have this little device with the majority of the accumulated knowledge that we as humans have gathered over time and how it causes us all to feel detached from life in real time because we have entirely too much access.

records.title: Forget About Me
records.note:
This is my genesis music NFT which is very special to me as it's a full circle moment of my NFT journey over the past year -- and it all started with this song.

Diplo, Durante, and I finished the production on "Forget About Me" in the summer of 2021 -- around the same time, I was working on developing my first NFTs that ended up being linked to this song. 

My first NFT drop was Decentraland compatible headphones that fans could use to listen to "Forget About Me" in an exclusive VIP room during my Decentraland Metaverse Festival performance in October, 2021. Inside the metaverse was the very first time this song was heard by fans, which is such an exciting idea to me. 

Shortly after this, I collaborated with the incredible FELT Zine on the Cocoa Cream Cake Puffer jacket. Flash forward a few months later, and now the cake theme ended up in the music video for this song.

When looking for the final collaborator for this record, I was not only drawn to Serwah Attafuah's style, but also her relationship with using music as a rebellion -- so I had to have her create the artwork for this song. When I got the artwork from Serwah it blew my mind. We then decided to expand on the single artwork, and created a 5 piece mini collection that became a beautiful example of what Black women in the industry can achieve. 

My genesis music NFT is the final piece of the puzzle, which marks a moment in history where my early supporters will be remembered forever. 

By investing in artists directly, you're investing in the world we want to build. In today's music industry, music is just invested in to be exploited. But Web3 gives world builders the ability to create in multiple avenues for the next generation of artists.

Music lovers and artists have been waiting for a moment like this where we're closer than ever, and together we can build a new world.

records.title: Crossed Our Hearts
records.note:
Even though the pandemic has been an emotional rollercoaster for me (as it has for most people), I’m not sure where my career would be if it hadn’t happened. Because of it, I was able to play a virtual festival called Brownies & Lemonade Open Aux which opened up a lot of doors for me. Since then, I’ve played 4 irl festivals, recently got off a US tour with RL Grime, and released with nearly all of my dream labels.

But even after all of those wins I couldn’t help feeling that something was missing—the magic in releasing music had become foreign to me. After getting involved with web3 and NFTs 12 months ago and observing some of my peers release their first projects, I realized the power of music NFTs and could feel that magic I once felt start to return. The community aspect and supportiveness (from artists and fans alike) in web3 is unlike anything I’ve ever been a part of. I believe that Sound is on the forefront of introducing a much needed shift in the music industry and I’m so excited to be a part of it.

In 2016 I began my career as a vocalist and found myself drawn to the thought of being able to produce and engineer my own music and vocals. After a year of watching YouTube videos and hiding out in my college dorm room making music, I decided to apply to a music production school called ICON Collective in LA and, within a year, I dropped out of nursing school and drove from Wisconsin to LA to start my music journey. To my surprise, the school only had a handful of women and I quickly learned the struggles of being a woman in a male-dominated industry. Throughout the last 6 years I’ve made it a priority of mine to make sure women are getting the credit they deserve and I’m excited to see a bit of a shift happening in that sense. There are so many incredible women producers, vocalists, engineers, and DJs, especially POC women, in the scene that are getting the recognition they deserve and I hope to see this continue to progress. Crossed Our Hearts is produced, written, recorded, mixed, and mastered by me. It’s just one of a number of self-produced tracks I’ve released but it marks my first music NFT. This song is about moving on from something I once thought was forever.

records.title: HOME AWAY FROM HOME
records.note:
I believe in sanctuary and that everyone is capable of building their own personal oasis. I find it important in times likes these to be very aware of who you invite into your space and for them to know the importance of that invitation. When I was writing this song I could see moving pictures with every line that came to my mind. I thought of how most scenarios within the dynamic of lovers make it so you are dependent on one another. It is very hard to be independent and still feel a sense of purpose in a relationship. I find value in the teachings and in the experiences. I could see the tension of two people and how we sometimes push each other away by being afraid separation. Not acknowledging that we bring power to each other by supporting each others space when needed. So when I stepped in front of the mic and made time to speak out this view it was not hard. 

“I like the feng shui just the way you see it” symbolized more that its actual meaning. I was speaking on I have a sense of self here and I wouldn’t like it much if you weren’t first accepting of it. I’ve been in relationships in the past where I changed to make someones life easier but it ultimately made me less of myself. This song is like a freedom song and a true connection song championing that there is no desperation in growth. 

I remember sitting with K. Roosevelt as we initially started to make this record and after we found a scape we liked, the words started to flow. I am not even sure I wrote the words down. A kind of vulnerability I want to continue to be known for. A kind of transparency that I feel creates the moments that make life , ART. Thank you for another opportunity to share truths. I HOPE YOU LIKE THE SONG.

records.title: Over U
records.note:
It’s been a period of change and growth. Like other artists, most of my shows were cancelled (i.e. first Australia tour, biggest Asia tour to date) and I began to spiral, struggling to find inspiration: on top of that, I ended a seven year relationship. But sometimes to find your future, you have to let go of the past. 

I stumbled into this new world called web3, with its vibrant communities and tech and memes. As I delved deeper, inspired by its creativity and energy, I realized that as artists, autonomy is all we have.       For so long, musicians have been sold a snake oil game, that there’s only one way to win - breakout hit, go viral on social media, major label deal, arena tour - but there are also serious pitfalls, including the trap of getting handcuffed and losing creative control of our vision while reducing the value of our art to pennies. After some thought (and encouragement from a couple friends) I said no thanks, walking away from a traditional three album record deal that was on the table. I decided to bet on myself on this new playing field with limitless potential.

‘Over U’ is the beginning of that journey - as the first single from my next EP. It is a declaration that the past is done with and a celebration of all to come, a party record to sweat it out and kick off a new year. I hope it brings a smile to your face.

records.title: First In The Fam
records.note:
For those who don't know, my first name is Heno but my full name is "Yihenew" which in Amharic means "This Is It." As the youngest of 4 in my family, my parents would often celebrate that I would be successful one day; early on laying the foundation of what manifestation would prove to be in my life. Although my life panned out differently than what they had intended, a hard veer from a promising route to medical school while attending Howard University, to living on my own terms as a full-time creative and now embracing Web3, the desire for more was always present but the curiosity to critically question— and sometimes even challenge— everything around me was growing exponentially. 

A big part of making decisions is also having to live with the ramifications of those decisions. Choosing this artist life isn’t for the faint-hearted. It took a lot of sacrifice, pain, guts, blood, sweat, tears + more to weather the storm; through the good and the bad. But I realized a long time ago that you simply can’t make everybody happy when you’re in pursuit of your dreams and sometimes you just got to accept that cold truth. That’s why the second part of this song hits as hard as it does for me every time I hear it. I had to let go of the idea of gaining my family’s support despite making the decision to go against what they wanted for me. Overtime, I’ve made peace with some of my family, at least the ones that still matter to me, and have been the subject of celebration back in my hometown in Maryland. 

This record is for any first generation immigrant that has had to deal with the pressure of being successful and taking care of your family. For the promises we make and for those working to follow through on all of them, to the people working hard to break generational curses, to those taking care of your family and honoring them in what you do, this record is for you.

records.title: NEYBORS (feat. Elujay & J.Robb)
records.note:
“NEYBORS” is about giving your undivided attention to that special someone & sharing those intimate moments uninterrupted. 

I’ve lived in settings where I’ve had annoying neighbors either above/below me or next door ask me to either turn down the volume when I’m playing music or keep the general volume down when having guests over. But nothing is more annoying when that happens while trying to spend quality time with your significant other. Those intimate moments can completely take your focus away from everything else in the world. Sometimes it can all feel therapeutic or even euphoric; where you don’t even need to speak & can just exist together.

I wanted to end the summer on an upbeat and feel-good vibe as I gear up for the release of my next EP. This was actually the first record that J.Robb played me out of a pack when he and Elujay both came over to my house in LA to kick it. As soon as I heard it I knew it was special because I felt like both the production and the parts Elujay had laid were perfect. I ended up writing both my verses that same day and recorded them the next day.

One of the best things you can provide your significant other is undivided attention. The feeling of being wanted, desired, and/or having a hold on someone, in THIS DAY AND AGE, is saying a lot. I think it’s the little things like being present when spending time with your partner that makes those moments feel like heaven. It shows an intention is being made & keeps that energy on a high. 

“NEYBORS” will be on all platforms on Tuesday, September 6th.

records.title: Bliss
records.note:
I wrote this song near the beginning of the pandemic. ‘Bliss’, like all songs that I write, encapsulates a moment in time. Writing songs is my personal way of keeping a diary. In a time of such chaos and uncertainty, the way that I’ve found to stay sane is to look inwards and tap into the fundamental neural circuitry that we all have. ‘Bliss’ is an exercise in staying true to my own tastes and experiences. The human experience is a constant struggle to achieve a state of bliss. 

I naturally gravitate towards experimentation and novelty. The strange filter patterns and sounds of the main synth lines were borne through countless hours of mixing and matching different parameters of different synthesizers. It is through this same ethos that pushed me towards the world of Web3 and sound.xyz is a perfect partner for me to explore the space with. 

Though the song represents a specific time and place for me, the meaning of it is obviously subjective to whoever listens. I hope that whoever takes the time to listen to it is able to add these frequencies to their own personal life journey and interpret it however they see fit.

records.title: Suffer In Silence
records.note:
"Suffer In Silence" was a record that was originally intended to be on my forthcoming album, I'm Tired of Being Hypersurveilled", but I chose to take it off because I felt like this song stood better alone.

Being a first generation Ethiopian-Eritrean growing up in Takoma Park, MD, it was normal to not speak much on the things we dealt with internally; whether it's due to not wanting to burden anyone, not wanting to be labeled with any stigma, not wanting to appear weak, or simply not having anyone to talk to. We don't say what is wrong, until it is way too late. We hold back on saying what we want, or the way we would like things to be. I used to suffer with substance abuse and suicidal thoughts issues trying to suppress myself in a world where everyone was taught to be afraid of me. It forced me to shrink in rooms I was very deserving to be in but felt the need to make others comfortable by being a lesser version of myself. This is after years of trauma dealing with adversity in many shapes and forms; some of which stem from street life and the over-policing of my community. I experienced a lot of racial profiling, being dragged by my dreads in the street and beaten, had a knee on my neck with a dislocated shoulder, illegal police break-ins into my home with no warrant, guns drawn at me on several occasions, and more - all while just trying to exist.

Feeling sad or numb doesn't mean that you are a weak person; matter of fact, it makes you more human if anything. Unfortunately, many people are unable to cope up with mental illnesses such as depression & anxiety (which I still deal with on/off) because they are scared or embarrassed to get the help that they need. In my culture these issues are things I hope to normalize speaking up about. I think it comes from a generational trauma of being under suppressive governments that made speaking up the most dangerous thing anyone could do - in both Ethiopia & America.

Through this journey of speaking up about my issues, unapologetically sharing my truths, and having these conversations, I found a deeper appreciation for life, more self love, and a heightened sense of gratitude in what already IS rather than stressing about stuff that ISN'T. May this song be a reminder that we aren't defined by our adversity, but by how we deal with that adversity; whether we let it block our path or push on through. No one should have to suffer in silence.

Just know that you are more than enough.
.
.
.

records.title: Metamorphosis
records.note:
The song “Metamorphosis” was originally inspired by a book by Franz Kafka, where a salesman named Gregor wakes up one morning to discover he has morphed into a huge bug. He struggles with this new realization and traps himself in his room while his family, who is dependent on him, struggles to make ends meet.

I didn’t want to write a song about a giant roach, because… gross. However I was extremely intrigued by the concept of evolving into a new existence that those closest to you cannot identify until some major breakthrough or shedding of self has been made. Even in this identification, they lose interest and you could lose yourself. 

I have found myself in this predicament many times, where I lost sight of my goals for the betterment and pleasing of others, leaving me burnt out. When I started shifting my energy and studying the boundaries I had originally set up to protect me, I saw that they were no longer serving me. As I shed them, I saw my circles shift. I saw my community change, diminish, then flourish. My creativity blossomed, once I started allowing myself time to live for myself. 

This track is written, produced, performed and engineered by myself using Ableton. The lil bug sounding sample is my own voice. Hopefully in listening you will find inspiration for transformation.

records.title: As Of Recent
records.note:
I'm starting 2022 off on the right foot by premiering my new song "As Of Recent" here on Sound. This record (that I wrote & produced) is a feel good summation of what life has been over the last few months. Before my introduction and entry into Web3, my life was completely different. 

This music journey has put me through all the trials and tribulations I can think of. I’ve been very nomadic in nature the last few years which that has put me through a lot of uncomfortable situations. From being homeless & couch surfing, working multiple jobs to save up & stay afloat, mental health battles, deaths of close family/friends, harassment by law enforcement, & that’s just the tip of the iceberg. There have been many times I could have given up but the presence of a higher power & sheer resiliency have kept me on the path I’m on; even in the eye of the storm. They don’t often see the sacrifices needed to be made in order to succeed beyond what one can fathom but finding comfort in the uncomfortable has allowed me to really transcend in a way & embrace it all head on; in psychology, they tend to refer to this as post-traumatic growth. 

I feel like dealing with adversity not only makes us stronger when dealing with negative things but can also help us appreciate the positive ones; even increasing our overall satisfaction with life. It’s allowed me to be more empathetic to others, build self efficacy, & also reassess stress as more of a challenge to problem solve rather than be discouraged. Web3 has opened up a whole new world for so many, and I'm blessed to be in a space where my craft, passion, & livelihood has been appreciated/valued in a way that has inspired me in a different way. 

As of recent, the air feels fresher. Food has been tasting better. My skin has been glowing. The hard work has been paying off. The gratitude is real as fuck. The intention is sincere. The vision is clear. And the future is very bright. 

I've been finding a deeper appreciation for life as of recent, hence the title...

records.title: better
records.note:
i make music for humans that are constantly evolving. constantly learning, unlearning, and striving to be better. not in search for perfection, but in search of progression, and a life that reflects our hearts' greatest desires. 

in the same way that caterpillars become butterflies, i believe that we evolve, too. the covid-19 pandemic has served as a chrysalis phase for me. it gifted me with time to look internally and figure out who i wanted to be and how i wanted to show up in the world. and in that search, i found truths i could no longer ignore. the main truth was this: the web2 music industry was killing me. emotionally, spiritually, mentally, physically. it was breaking me. the feeling of being unseen. the betrayal i was told to get used to. it broke my heart and my spirit. it was a hamster wheel that, if i'm honest, i knew i no longer had the stamina for. the person i'd have to become in order to be successful, the values i'd have to ignore, the box i'd have to fit in— especially as a black woman— would have left me unrecognizable to myself. i couldn't chance that. so i reevaluated things. i took a step away and changed things. i changed me. i bettered me. and then i found web3. 

when people see my NFT success, they think that NFTs are what changed my life. and although they have in many ways, my NFT success is merely the result of the betterment i chose to make internally. and that's what this song "better" is about. a highlight reel of what those changes were for me, and a depiction of where those changes led me. 

i hope this upbeat track produced by kaelin ellis gets you up out of your seat. i hope this vibrant cover illustrated by khalidah c reminds you of your own light. and i hope that you keep choosing betterment; even when it's hard.

this is one of the best songs i've ever written. so excited to share.

with peace,
iman europe

records.title: If You Tried ft VÉRITÉ
records.note:
If You Tried - TOMI x VÉRITÉ

Sometimes we have to leave everything behind in order to evolve. My name is Pam Autuori, and I perform under the name TOMI. 

Music has always been my therapy; it’s the voice I can rely on when I need clarity, a good vent, or just an outlet to be free from the world we live in. Growing up as a queer kid in the suburbs, I relied on music as a means to process my identity and I started TOMI to have a place I could go where I didn’t have to chase fads, I could chase myself. 

I met VÉRITÉ soon after I started TOMI. I had been watching her success and was in awe of her work ethic and ability to bring her life experiences into her music so seamlessly and honestly. After our initial meeting I knew we had to collaborate. She instantly changed my perspective on how to approach the music industry and the diligence it takes to be the best version of oneself. When she dove headfirst into web3, I knew it was the next horizon for independent artists.

I have an almost too typical music industry story…signing away my rights, losing the autonomy over my art and finding myself in a position where I was stuck between a bad record deal and forward momentum. “If You Tried” is a song about relieving oneself of blame and moving forward - independent, wiser and stronger. This song gave me a voice when I felt like mine had been signed away.

Writing and producing “If You Tried” felt like an exhale, as if I had finally let out a breath I had been holding in for so long. Releasing her into the world through sound.xyz and entering a completely new world of possibility for how I create, distribute and experiment with my music feels electric, like there are no limits to what I am capable of. This is the way music should be released and the way it should be heard without the fluff and rat race of the music industry we’ve come to know. Web3 is a rare way to connect with people all over the world, metaverse and beyond and I am thrilled to be a part of this new adventure. 

Thank you for listening to “If You Tried” and I hope it brings you a feeling of empowerment and strength. Until next time…

records.title: Monday - Friday
records.note:
I wrote, produced, and engineered this song at my home studio in Las Vegas. Often times I finish songs quickly, but "Monday - Friday" is an outlier that took months. I pushed myself creatively on this song, and I think that's why I've grown so attached to it.

The intro begins with drowsy chords and an entrancing four on the floor kick pattern. Before things become stale the beat quickly transforms into hard hitting halftime drums with glitched music to kick off a verse. Bouncing back and forth between grooves isn't very common, and in my opinion it's what makes this song stand out. I lyrically start describing what my week was looking like - Uber drivers mistaking me for drug dealing because I have cash from rap... My ex ringing me about nothing while I'm in the middle of something important... Rolling 3 SUVs deep full of friends so it looks like we're in a black car convoy... 

I play Mon - Fri" when I want to get in the zone. I had to sacrifice a lot to get to where I'm at, and this song is a testament that I shouldn't be afraid to remind people of the mountains I've climbed to get here.

I went through the major label industry and came out the other end daunted and struggling to connect with the world I had once created from. It has given me back the voice I felt I had lost and given me infinite possibilities to experiment and reach higher than I ever have before.

I wrote “Wild, Wild River” about searching for a feeling just out of reach. It’s about finding strength within yourself when you feel lost or out of control. It’s a reminder that what we are searching for can be found if we slow down and look inward. I wrote this song at a time of loss in my life and it helped me find the power within myself to continue on - stronger and braver than before.

Music is my way of giving back to the community that held me up through all of my growing-pain years. I will forever be grateful for the songs and the people who have paved the way before me and I hope this song can shine a light for those who feel lost in this wild, wild world.

Not surprisingly this song fell into that category and was written in just under 30 minutes. It's fully written and produced by me.

I went a bit more aggressive on the lyrical content while adding pretty melodic moments to offset the seriousness of the song. "Light Show" is best played when you need a confidence boost. I detail times where I've let grudges slide and took the highroad, and also reflect on the fact that putting my pain out in the open is what's allowed me to grow and reach levels of success as an artist. It's 100% accurate when I state "I spent hard earned cash just to keep this up, I spent blood sweat and tears just to keep this going". 

This song is a window into my life, and I hope you can use this shit as a tool to let loose and rage.

records.title: ALAMO
records.note:
Recently I've realized that I really miss making dance music. I really miss putting things out that are fun and feel good. When I started "Alamo", I instantly locked myself into the project and let everything out. It's a little chaotic, but playful. 

Growing up listening lots of breakbeats and funk, I always envision images of people of the past dancing. 

Music that speaks to you can really evoke memories or fictional stories in your head. Music that really speaks to you might generate a new story each time you listen to it again. I have had so many great conversations with friends about what they see in their heads when they listen to certain songs.

Here's a short summary of a vision I'm seeing now while listening to "Alamo":

It's 2050...

Imagine you're with your best friend in a drop top in the desert. You don't recognize your best friend, for some reason, but you know they're your best friend.

Somehow it's getting darker in the sky even though it's in the middle of the day and also getting hotter. Both of you start sweating buckets and the car is also bunny hopping up and down, side to side.

You both decide to take off your t-shirts, but when each t-shirt is removed another one is there in its place. This keeps going on and you decide to just keep driving and smoking. You forget about taking off the t-shirts, because there are vampires next to your car chasing you. You have absolutely no way of surviving unless you turn on your hyper thrusters and blast off to the Alamo - somewhere warmer and sunnier. 

Somehow it doesn't take that long for both of you to get close to the Alamo. Gas prices are nonexistent in 2050, as cars are mostly urine-powered. The sun comes out when you both arrive at the Alamo and things cool off. You put on hoodies. Everything fades to black.

- The end.

Thank you for reading & listening. Hope this song makes you do the dancing and brings you joy.

records.title: Climb (feat. Phinisey)
records.note:
Phinisey and I write the wildest, weirdest songs together. This is the first one we're releasing unto the world.

We met in LA back in 2019 when I was living out there. We instantly hit it off for our shared sense of just making whatever. Nothing needed to make sense, fit a specific container or vibe. We'd just jam. 

Phinisey is crazily talented — production, songwriting, singing, mixing, engineering. Dude does it all. We didn't reopen Climb for a long time after our initial session writing it. But we'd always play it back and be like "damn, this really goes".

It wasn't until a session over zoom during the pandemic when I was like "what if you just sing the lyrics from my first verse as the second verse, and we make this song a joint release?" Phinisey laid down the vocals and naturally crushed it. 

Finally, the canonical version of Climb was born. Enjoy..

records.title: JUNGLE
records.note:
All of the music that I write is extremely autobiographical. My goal is always to dig deeper within myself because that’s where I feel everything starts when it comes to change in the world. It always begins within ourselves, I know the more transparent I can be with my experiences the more I can affect the world in a positive manner. I don’t open up too much so my music is almost like public therapy for me. 

This song captures my story from the beginning, my current lifestyle, and my future goals. When I think about my history, my ancestry, and my roots I feel a deep sense of pride and am very thankful for where I am today. Most of us are more privileged than we realize, especially by simply having access to computers as well as having the knowledge and foresight to be using them in this way... ie. Web3 etc. 

I’ve been waiting for the right time to drop this one as it is very special to me, and I hope everyone else feels the vibes and raw emotion in it as well.

records.title: The AbJonian Suite, Vol. II (Demo Mix)
records.collection: The AbJonian Suite, Vol. II (Demo Mix)
records.note:
I first dropped the original "AbJonian Suite" under the Potholes In My Blog internet label during the infamous blog era (you can find the original here: https://potholesmusic.bandcamp.com/album/the-abjonian-suite). It was originally meant to serve as just a way to get off my beats in a way that forced the listener to listen to and enjoy a project as a whole. Instead, it re-framed for me how I would arrange my future projects, show my evolution as a producer to the world in an organized fashion, and position myself as more than just a beat maker, but a music artist and bonafide music producer, one of the caliber I sought so long to prove I was. From it, I landed many gigs not just playing my own music, but playing sets and mixing music fully the way I imagined it, and allowed me to bend the rules in rooms, on stages in front of both tens and hundreds, to thousands of people to make them move, make them feel something and hear something like never before (at least the way I see it, haha!)

This is really just a snapshot of where I am right now musically, just like the last one was, a humble contribution to the musical conversation at large, and a statement to my tribe of colleagues, idols of mine and mentees of mine alike, of who I am as a musician and producer as well. For the listener, the supporter, the fanatics of mine, however, it's a gift to you all, and a reminder that there is always more coming soon... ✊🏽

records.title: Reasons
records.note:
I wrote and produced Reasons as a just a fun song about why I be low key to be honest. A lot of time in the entertainment industry, ppl equate your fame level with your quality of life. But most of the ppl I look up to who have what I consider to be a high quality of life aren’t necessarily famous. I’ve found when you keep your wins & happiness private it tends to last longer. 

Basically all forces of power I’ve been involved in from management to labels are motivated to keep you ignorant enough about business, but worth it just enough so you keep creating for them. It’s a lot easier and faster to make the most $ off someone's back the more ignorant they are in the traditional industry. I’d say I’ve gotten got in every way possible, from bad deals, stolen ideas, not paid after a sold out tour, etc. But all of that taught me so much about business. I took some of my $ invested in real estate and did some good flips w/ my manager Jay, bought myself outta bad deals and learned how to fund my lifestyle and career completely outside of the traditional industry. Through real estate development and investing, I’m also able to give and hire POC through my businesses and my non profit "Yebo Life". 

The meme coins and Wall Street Bets stocks don’t hurt either. In our label, Mogul Sound Music, we want our artists to be as knowledgeable as possible about business and investing because it helps all of us get sharper. The more our artists know, the more they succeed, and the more responsibility they put on themselves to be great.

records.title: FRAGMENTS
records.note:
Sometimes when something happens in life and you feel like everything is falling to pieces, it’s hard to keep up with the thoughts of being broken. Sometimes things aren’t really that bad, but memories of the past can haunt you for a long time. It’s easy to get stuck thinking about “what ifs”. When you put a lot of love, time & energy into someone or something and they disappear from your life, you can feel hollow. But then you heal.. because you have to. It might take a lot of time, but you still have to try. Maybe some of you can relate. This piece is about the journey from Hurt.. to Letting go.. to Focusing on the present. 

I don't know what else to say. My heart broke - and I got fucked up. This is what it sounds like when you get fucked up. But I don't blame anyone.

Thanks for listening. I'm glad you could hear me cry.

records.title: Buzzin
records.note:
This song is about getting up and following your dreams... The search for something greater. This applies specifically to my life, being a first generation immigrant, moving around a lot as a kid, and being an artist/entrepreneur. I've always been on a search for something bigger than myself. My very conception was between 2 people who left their native countries of Tanzania and South Africa, to fly across the ocean in search of something more. 

There's a "Buzzin" feeling you get when you know your potential is greater than your physical environment. I think a lot of small towners and midwesterners who seek to make an impact in the world can feel me as well. After Brady Watt and I connected we finished this song probably in 2 hours tops, and he played every instrument on it. This was really fun to me because I came up performing to a band way before I ever had a DJ. A band / natural instrument setting is probably the most natural way for me to write and perform. 

I moved around mainly out of necessity as a child, but as a young man I had the pleasure of choosing to live in some of the greatest cities in the world. What's crazy is that everything came full circle. Everything I learned from all of the cultures and places I've been, have taught me how to give back, build, and make my hometown of St. Paul, Minnesota a greater place to live for myself and my whole community.

records.title: you're invited (ft. Steve Davit)
records.note:
our first album in four years comes out later this week and we're so excited we decided to share one more taste of it with you all...

why can't we just pretend, for a moment, that we're in a crowded sweaty venue in a post-Covid world...glittering chandeliers hang from the ceilings...audience members are dressed to the 9s...you're with your favorite people in the world...and the band plays this song.

you're invited is our first Sound release with a feature, and it's only right that it's from Steve Davit, our esteemed saxophonist. if you've ever seen us live, you know his impact. Steve went to middle school and high school with us and has toured with us since the very beginning. His energy is a vital component of the Marian Hill cocktail and quite frankly he is simply the saxiest man in town. 

we love the energy of this song and we hope you will too. thank you for spending some of your day appreciating it. we are so grateful to each and every one of you.

yours,

MH

records.title: i tried, fam.
records.note:
I've been back and forth for a long time now on what my next move in life is gonna be, which has coincided with some setbacks on many levels recently that effectively solidified that I had to make it now, or I never would.

Long story short, I'm going back to school to get my Master's degree in music, with the plan to teach/educate folks about electronic music from a Black perspective, and our history in revolutionizing all music with just a handful of musical devices and techniques, or through developing musical styles that dominate popular music to this day.

I digress, though: I've been feeling defeated until recently because I failed elsewhere in my life. I tried, really hard, but maybe just not hard enough. I'm tired. Exhausted. Sometimes from just being a Black man living in this world we live in, most times from just not being where I expected to be by now, which is really where the idea of this song originated.

This is for my peoples who are ready to give up. To stop chasing for a minute, and to accept where you're at and how you feel, instead of propping up your ego and your pride, and say out loud that you really did try. We all have, we've all been there, too, so you're not alone, and this isn't the end. Enjoy it while you can, enjoy it here in this moment I created, and find catharsis in knowing you have to fail at some point, to one day eventually succeed. 

Right?

Right...

records.title: Pray for Health
records.note: Pray for Heal was born when a woman who barely spoke any English approached me after jumping off the Amtrak train in 2014, asking me to help her connect with her charter bus. I was in the midst of that situation at the time when two guys (at the same bus stop) who were fans of my music approached me. It was in those darkest days that I found a lot of light in an uncertain situation. They went as far as even asking for pictures with me, and I regained some confidence after that experience and I started to realize that I have this talent for a reason. Felt like I was saved that night!

records.title: Lifted Demons
records.note:
Last year was a year full of high anxiety and depression. It took a strain on my mental, and for the longest time I haven’t been able to cry, no matter the situation that emotion was completely cutoff! After multiple trips to help deal with my emotions it felt like I unlocked a whole new part of myself!

I managed to create Lifted Demons out of darkness and this record made me feel light, it made me want to jump around and enjoy myself again. Like, it literally had been so long since I’ve seen my true self and once I did it felt like my demons had been lifted!

“It’s been a long time since I seen you man, fuck is going on”

We have all dealt and maybe are still dealing with some type of darkness. I’m here to tell you keep fighting, no matter the battle. You have only yourself to prove something to!

records.title: remember me
records.note:
This will be the first song on our first album in 4 years. 

It almost didn’t happen. 

Before the pandemic we had gotten so exhausted and jaded for a moment it felt like we might walk away. Then the world ended. And for the first time in 8 years we were apart. In those lost months we remembered how much Marian Hill means to us, and means to all of you. How the connection we find through our music is literally magic. And we knew we needed to finish this record.

Marian Hill gave both of us the lives we'd always dreamed of, and kept us going during the worst year of our lives. When Samantha found herself turning 30 in her childhood bedroom and Jeremy suffered an onset of chronic pain in both of his wrists, the music we made gave us moments of joy to hold onto in a world full of uncertainty. For a few moments each day, we could get lost in a song, and pretend we were playing it for you.

This song in some ways feels like a message from that time to eternity. When we started thinking of the lyrics we were really thinking about us as a band, us as songwriters...will we be remembered? Do people still care? Will anyone care in 5 years, 10 years, 20 years?

It’s also about wondering if an ex will remember you once the relationship is far in the rearview.

And about if any of our art will last as climate change escalates to world-ending levels.

When you listen to this song, you are with us, wherever you are. 

We invite you to share your own memories in the comments - together we’ll build a wall of memories forever immortalized through music.

someday when everything’s underwater
and all our memories are forgotten
there’s nothing
as far as you can see
i wonder in all that…
is there a trace of me?

will you remember me?

records.title: 5:55am.
records.note:
This track is for all of my peoples who have to wake up before the sun comes up to make ends meet, the early risers who found their beat to start the grind for the life that they want, a soundtrack to contemplate your next move, whether it’s to secure the bag, realize your dreams, or just tear up the asphalt to as you dance your way to the finish line, when the rest of the world is seemingly non-existent. As if there was no one else but you out there…

I wrote this during the pandemic, working as an essential worker the entire time, something I was not accustomed to as a career musician/DJ/producer for so long before. I thought for a while I couldn’t even make the same music as before, because I wasn’t living like I used to, head in the proverbial clouds and blessed to do what I love for a living. I had a whole different grind, a different perspective that put me out of my usual, ideal state of mind, that working 40+ hours a week wasn’t going to get me to.

Instead, though, I learned over time how much this motivated me to persevere, be patient, and wait for my next “cubic centimeter of chance” as I call it, the chance for me to break back through and find momentum, back into that state of mind that brought me the musical workflow I became successful with.

Dance Like No One Else Exists (or “5:55am”, the time I remember finishing this beat) is me, dancing the dance of the early grinder, ready to take it all on so I can get to my real work, making music that moves people, and reminds them that you and you alone can move mountains, let alone yourself. So dance like no else exists, move to your own beat, and don’t ever forget who you know and believe you are.

This one is for my late father who passed last April, Gary Nash, my inspiration to keep making music everyday, any way I can, anywhere I’m at.

Rest in peace, Pops…

records.title: Bittersweet (w/ DEEGAN)
records.note:
I met DEEGAN my first week living in Los Angeles. I was at a show watching a friend perform when I got a tap on the shoulder - I thought I was going to run into one of my other friends who recently moved cross country with me but instead I was greeted by a total stranger. He introduced himself and I immediately recognized him after having worked with his cousin months prior.

The next day I did a deep dive on his catalog and invited him over to my place for a session. I remember being blown away by the weird noises he could produce with just his voice alone. I realized he was the type of creative that wouldn't try to structure out the perfect song - he would let me do whatever I wanted to do. And creatively that's exactly what I needed. 

Over the years DEEGAN and I have worked on so many records together. From our early days making bleeps and bloops on my computer to his 2 features on Overstimulated, to the writing camp I put together in Malibu, DEEGAN has consistently been one of my favorite people to work with - not only for his musical abilities - but for his undeniable personality that lights up every room he's in. 

Bittersweet is a record that I started on last summer and sent to DEEGAN at the end of last year. When I was looking for a song to drop on Sound, I came across this topline but the production felt outdated. I ended up manically sitting with it for 72 hours and this is the result that came out. It's a preview of my new direction sonically.

This song is about the mixed emotions one feels after a breakup: The happiness of not having to deal with their toxic behavior anymore, and the sadness in losing all of the good parts about them.

records.title: Barely Situated
records.note:
Rome and I have never actually met, but I know about dude and his music, which I've appreciated from afar until now. It took the rise of music NFTs and a group chat to land us on some tracks together finally, and this is one of soon to be many that we hope to release for your listening pleasure, which we named "Barely Situated". I figured for this release, something special I can do is give away all my royalties from this release to another Black artist (from any discipline, music or not) looking to get a headstart in the NFT space, so upon selling out all editions of this track, I'll be picking whoever can plead their case best, however they can reach me. My DMs are open, my mentions are available, I wanna uplift you the way this community, space, platform and tool has uplifted and motivated me to make the best art I can...

Peace and power to all,
Ab ✊🏽

records.title: Trippin Out
records.note:
This is the oldest song on our upcoming album "why can’t we just pretend?"

We wrote it exactly three years ago during one of the sessions for our "was it not" EP. 

We started writing it in a way we never had before - in the room, no beat.  Sam sang a melody as Jeremy snapped his fingers softly. And then we just had fun.

"Trippin out" felt too weird for the EP. Its hard to justify a strange intense record without a catchy chorus on a five song project in the streaming era. Through the years our most experimental songs have often seen the fewest streams. So we added it to the pile of oddball MH outtakes and moved on.

The following year as we put together our fourth album in the middle of a global pandemic we found ourselves compiling a list of song contenders and stumbled back onto "Trippin Out". It was still perhaps the strangest thing we’d ever made. And together we decided that no matter what anybody else said, this song needed to be on our album. 

We are so grateful to platforms like Sound for building a music experience where peculiar curiosities can flourish. We hope you enjoy this ear candy as much as we do - thank u, as always, for listening.

records.title: Heart Attack (original version)
records.note:
Heart attack came about from three separate events that all had the same effect on me more or less. I’d really hurt the girl I was seeing in the months she was away, and I went to her house to talk through everything. I realized pretty quickly it wasn’t going to be a favorable discussion though, she’d made up her mind and I wasn’t in any place to try to convince her otherwise, so I left with my eyes full of water and cried in the car for the better part of an hour. Weeks went by without seeing her, but then I eventually did at a friends birthday and it was like getting sledge hammered in the chest. I’d started seeing someone else around that time, which in hindsight was really irresponsible because my heart wasn’t nearly settled, so it just led to a lot more stupid sadness for everyone involved.  Really all this music from the first half of Cherry is just the product of me being an idiot boy that couldn’t see beyond his own nose too well. Like this song is so sad but you can’t really pity someone that orchestrated their own pain. But don’t worry, the room gets brighter the further you walk into it and we have a lot of room left.

This is the version of Heart Attack I was originally going to go with before I sat with it for a few weeks and completely reproduced it from the ground up. It didn’t feel right to not have this version exist somewhere so I’m glad you’ll have it here. All holders of this drop will be airdropped an edition of the final version when it’s released on my site later this year.

records.title: Honey
records.note:
Ever since moving to Los Angeles I've had the pleasure of doing a bunch of sessions with talented vocalists. The process has taught me how to be comfortable in a room and make people feel ready to record, all while trying to be quick on my feet as a producer and catch a vibe with the artist I'm working with.

Over the past few months I've realized that most of the music I've made has been in sessions. And while I love vocal-driven music, I haven't really had the chance to sit back and do my own instrumental production experiments. When I look back on how I got started in music, so much of it was by myself sitting in a room twisting knobs and making odd sounds.

Honey is me taking a step back in that direction - it's a science experiment of a song that serves as my reminder to let go and have fun producing and to not take myself so seriously.

records.title: black eyes (with Mara Anne)
records.note:
These are the words I want to say when I float away and leave my body behind. 

Time dissipates when I am dancing. My movement encapsulates the interconnectedness of memory, instinct, emotion, and truth. But when the sweat dries and the clocks start up again, my identity can become distorted and blurred. Regret, guilt, fear, and loss flood my mind, ripping me away from the love that colors my life.

This is disassociating for me; I am no longer in control of my body, words, or feelings and I am a shell with empty eyes. My mind hovers and every conversation is empty. My loved ones feel abandoned while we are sitting right across from one another. I wrote these lyrics while fighting a dissociative episode and I managed to come back to myself through making my experience tangible and real with words and sound.

This song is a reclamation of myself. When I’m ready to become real again, patient love is always there to welcome me back home.

records.title: CHILDHOOD
records.note:
A lot has happened these past few years. Some things beautiful, most things painful, but all of it necessary. 

I've given much thought to the words I want to say here and if there are any that could possibly convey what I feel. For a long time it felt nearly impossible to find any words. I had to go through hell and back before learning how to navigate the turbulence of my sea of emotions. On that journey I found that creation was always my compass. Then my son was born, and he became my reason to stay. 

Almost all of my life has been spent creating things to be my anchor. It's my way of making sense of a world that feels alien to me, to process my experiences and to connect with people. Connecting has always been the thing I've desired most, and in my immaturity I sacrificed a lot of myself to have it. From my mind and my body, to my time, integrity and emotions.      
I lost many things in my pursuit of a connection, hurting myself and others in the process. A scared kid pretending to know everything. 

My childhood is where I stayed.

I wrote those words in the summer of 2017 during a period of severely exploitive label deals, poor management, a terrible break up and my own narcissistic and toxic self-destructive behavior destroying everything around me. 

My childhood was where I went to escape, reminiscing on the beauty and ignorance of being oblivious. And for a while it was safe. 

But life went on and I had abandoned those words and sentiment for years, blind to how important they really were. When I eventually found my way back to them, they had embodied a completely new and much more emotional meaning. They were no longer a door, but a mirror instead.

And when my son began his own childhood, that changed everything. 

The love of my life, our greatest creation and the most perfect gift from god. He gives me reason and resolve, the connection I've so desperately craved my entire life, a chance to break the cycle of pain that has plagued my life since I was his age. 

Still, nothing comes without hardship. 

I spent a long time fighting to know him, to be with him and to love him with everything I had in me at the time. But for reasons controllable and uncontrollable I was an ocean away from him for what felt like a lifetime. Logistics, lies and love lost orbited what was meant to be completely beautiful and so it seemed to be the end of the world, another failure of my own doing. But the love he filled me with didn't allow me to quit.

No matte

records.title: ample time
records.note:
Time is the greatest currency.

A lot of things lead us to believe that we don’t have much of it, but that couldn’t be further from the truth. We constantly see ourselves running out of time, losing it, instead of the beauty and experience that time gives us.

It’s true that you can never get time back, but what you spend that time on might just be infinitely more valuable.

For as long as I can remember I have always felt the clock ticking, never stopping, impartial to everyone. That filled me with fear. I tried for so long to get those seconds, minutes, hours and days back, wasting even more time in the process. It never worked.

I realise now that holding onto what has been lost will only offer you the same fate. Being lost in times gone by will have you learning the same lesson over and over again.

So now I decide to move forward, regardless of how much time has been lost, because there’s much more time left. How you choose to spend your time is your decision and yours alone… just remember that you have more than enough of it.

We all have ample time to love, lose, learn and live through.

records.title: Too Close
records.note:
I got into music later in life than most would assume. Being raised in an immigrant household, I didn’t have the opportunity to join a band, sing in a choir, or play multiple instruments. The entirety of my childhood was engulfed in school and sports, and I never really had the opportunity to pursue what I was passionate about as it didn’t fit the mold of what felt traditionally acceptable to my family.

I was introduced to music when I was seven. My brother - who is 15 years older than me - gave me his iPod classic, and for the first time I felt enamored. I was exposed to songs that most kids my age weren’t listening to, and in large part I attribute that iPod to getting me through elementary school. I was never a popular kid growing up, and it didn't help that I was struggling as I developed my English skills and navigating my way through a brand new culture. Most of the kids around me had seen life through a lens that was foreign to me, and that iPod helped me escape that reality and find meaning amongst the uncertainty. 

I knew then and there that I loved music, but I always approached it tangentially. In high school I became a self-proclaimed audio engineer, recording local artists in my bedroom closet. Eventually some of the artists I was recording asked me for beats but I wasn’t at all ready to recognize myself as an actual musician. I feared rejection and more importantly - being bad at something I aspired to be great at.

During my freshman year of college I decided to be intentional about what I wanted and take my life seriously. While studying pre-med and being an athlete, I decided to 180 my life’s trajectory and unapologetically go all in on learning how to make music. And I did this in the most extreme way possible: Every morning at 4 A.M. I'd start my day by taking notes on music production. I began my journey by taking every session I could across the street at Berklee School of Music - always being the worst producer in the room. I stopped caring about school entirely. My life became a big game of catchup - I lived on the margins to work on music in every crevice I could find, to catch up to the artists I was surrounding myself with. And while I’m grateful for those years of my life, they did come with a cost. 

All of us have bad habits, and mine is being selfish to a fault. Over the course of the past four years, I’ve cut so many people out of my life. Childhood friendships, relationships, and even family members have fallen by the ways

records.title: Sound
records.note: My Journey From Music To Crypto  Four years ago, I was a full-time music producer and global-traveling DJ. I had been working in music for nearly a decade, was getting millions of plays on streaming platforms, and had produced a couple songs that landed in the Billboard top 40. But despite having a career many people dream of, by 2016 I was feeling uneasy. My career had started to plateau and my attention was increasingly turning toward topics far afield from music, particularly the existential risks of technology.  To understand the source of my anxiety, it’s necessary to travel back to my childhood. I grew up watching a lot of Star Trek: The Next Generation with my dad. And looking back, the techno-optimist vision of Gene Roddenberry had a big influence on how I viewed human progress. My music tastes followed a similar theme. I vividly remember hearing Daft Punk’s Around The World the first time, and how excited I was when I bought my first synthesizer. This all led to a more serious interest in futurism in college. I started reading books like Ray Kurzweil’s The Singularity Is Near, and hard science fiction from authors like Stanislaw Lem, from whom I eventually took my DJ name, Gigamesh.  I released music and performed under that alias full time from 2008 onward, growing a modest global fan base. In the first two years, I achieved commercial success and started touring without a management team or agent. This was all possible thanks to the decentralized nature of pre-Spotify music discovery. I would post bootleg remixes and original songs on Soundcloud and send the links to a list of music blogs. The blogs would feed via RSS into aggregators like Hype Machine. There were very few gatekeepers so online music discovery was an organic, beautiful mess. It created a long tail of musicians like myself who wouldn’t have been able to make a living from it years earlier.  Another thing working to my benefit during the early years of my music career was that social media was still in its pre-monetization infancy. During this time, it was relatively easy for motivated, talented artists to cut through the noise and find a niche audience without doing constant self-promotion. Words like “content” and “algorithm” hadn’t become fixtures of every musician’s vocabulary.  By 2015, my career was cruising along at a steady clip but the road was getting bumpy.
